MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: HandsOn is a comprehensive simulation benchmark for dexterous manipulation, featuring diverse robotic platforms and tasks to evaluate generalization and sim-to-real transfer in manipulation skills.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: General-purpose manipulation requires reliable behavior across embodiments, objects, and task demands. We introduce HandsOn, a composable simulation platform and benchmark for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation. It supports five robotic arms, six dexterous hands, and approximately 200 rigid, articulated, and deformable assets in randomized scenes. The benchmark pairs 18,000 curated human demonstrations with 66 human-verified tasks: Core-50 supports demonstration-based learning and execution tests, while Transfer-16 evaluates asset and relation transfer, skill composition, and deformable manipulation without target-task training demonstrations. Qualitative real-robot rollouts illustrate sim-to-real transfer. Across diffusion, vision-language-action, world-action, and prompted VLM-based methods, the best trained multi-task policy achieves 29.1% Core-50 success. Without benchmark finetuning, GPT-6 using move_eef for palm-and-finger control achieves 5.2% on Core-50 and 1.9% on Transfer-16 over 660 trials. Trained-policy stage diagnostics expose failures in contact establishment, action coordination, and maintaining achieved goals, with additional sequencing errors in composed tasks. HandsOn provides a shared basis for investigating manipulation generalization and the limits of reliable physical interaction.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Xinhao Ji, Hui En Pang, Hao Li, Kairui Hu, Jiner Wang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: EgoXperience introduces a comprehensive framework for learning coherent egocentric representations from video, achieving significant improvements in joint reconstruction and object pose estimation.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Reconstructing human activity from egocentric video requires more than recovering individual 3D components: the observer's motion, surrounding geometry, and hand-object interactions must fit together in a consistent world. Achieving this coherence requires both joint reconstruction and aligned supervision, yet existing methods and datasets offer limited support for either. We present EgoXperience, a full-stack paradigm that addresses these needs through data collection, automatic annotation, unified modeling, and benchmarking. Central to EgoXperience is an automatic annotation engine, EgoX-Engine, that couples geometrically verified object tracking with SLAM-based world alignment, yielding consistent supervision for the camera, scene, hands, and objects. This yields EgoX-Data-6M, a 50-hour dataset of task-driven manipulation and locomotion within and across indoor and outdoor environments, with second-level task captions. We carefully select one hour across these activity categories as EgoX-Bench to evaluate joint reconstruction. To translate this supervision into reconstruction, we introduce EgoX, trained with EgoX-Data-6M and complementary annotations from additional public datasets. Given monocular egocentric video and first-frame object masks, our model achieves joint metric reconstruction of the camera, scene, hands, and objects in a shared world coordinate frame with a single forward pass. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across scene estimation and world-space hand-object pose recovery. Against the strongest evaluated baselines, EgoX reduces camera, hand, and depth errors by 68.9%, 65.6%, and 42.9%, and improves object pose scores by 28.0%.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Robotic Photography System based on Vision-Language-Action Model
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Song-Li Wu, Chubin Zhang, Wenbo Ding, Yansong Tang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: RoboPhoto-VLA is a unified framework for robotic photography that integrates perception, reasoning, and camera control to produce aesthetically pleasing images aligned with human preferences.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Modern robotic photography requires understanding photographic intent, planning camera motions, and producing aesthetically pleasing images in complex environments. We present RoboPhoto-VLA, a unified Vision-Language-Action framework that jointly models perception, reasoning, and camera control for autonomous robotic photography. RoboPhoto-VLA incorporates PhotoCoT for structured action planning and Aesthetic Direct Preference Optimization (ADPO) to align camera behaviors with human aesthetic preferences. To facilitate training and evaluation, we construct OpenPhotography, a robotic photography dataset with language-guided demonstrations. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that RoboPhoto-VLA produces photographs better aligned with human aesthetic preferences while generalizing effectively to unseen subjects, viewpoints, poses, and complex photographic instructions.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: UniW(A)M: A Unified Mixture-of-Experts Framework for World and World-Action Models
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Jingbo Xu, Jianjie Fang, Zhuohang Li, Zihao Song, Zhaolu Wang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: UniW(A)M is a unified framework that integrates world and world-action models using diffusion Transformers, enhancing prediction and control efficiency in robotic tasks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: World models (WMs) and world-action models (WAMs) focus on future world prediction and executable action generation, respectively. Although these models learn shared physical dynamics and interaction semantics from embodied trajectories, they are typically trained in isolation, which restricts knowledge reuse between prediction and control. The central challenge is therefore to develop a unified learning framework that shares these dynamics while preserving the distinct modeling capabilities required by each paradigm. We propose UniW(A)M, a mixture-of-experts world-(action) model built upon diffusion Transformers that unifies action-conditioned world modeling and diverse WAM variants. Shared experts capture common dynamics, while atomic capability experts are reused across interfaces so that each interface keeps its own conditional pathway. At deployment, a plug-in adaptive interface router (PAIR) learns from a small subset of target-task chunk scenarios to select a suitable WAM interface for each execution chunk, balancing task success and execution efficiency while keeping the backbone frozen. We evaluate UniW(A)M on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and three real-world manipulation tasks, where it achieves 88.3% average real-world success versus 76.7% for the strongest baseline. On WorldArena, it leads action-conditioned world modeling on all three tasks. AC-WM co-training contributes to action generation on every action interface and PAIR raises OOD success from 63.3% to 76.7%.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: LayerRoute: Action-Conditioned Mixture-of-Layers Routing for Vision-Language-Action Policies
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Zheng Lu, Haoran Liao, Wanqi Zhong, Yunhe Ni, Lijie Wang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: LayerRoute enhances Vision-Language-Action policies by enabling adaptive routing of visual-semantic representations and action states, improving performance with minimal parameter increase.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies leverage pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to guide action generation for robot control. VLMs provide hierarchical visual-semantic representations that evolve across layers, from local visual geometry to abstract, language-aligned semantics; different manipulation tasks may therefore require different mixtures of layer representations. Meanwhile, the action module maintains intermediate representations that evolve throughout action computation and may provide useful information for subsequent decisions. However, existing VLA interfaces offer limited flexibility in representation access: VLM information is exposed through fixed layer assignments for each action layer, while intermediate action states are only propagated implicitly through residual streams without explicit reuse. We introduce LayerRoute, an action-conditioned representation routing interface that enables adaptive access to VLM layers and action representations. The Layer Mixture Router dynamically forms mixtures of cached VLM representations, while Action-State Reread reuses earlier action representations. Across diverse simulation and real-world benchmarks, LayerRoute consistently improves StarVLA-$π$ and $π_{0.5}$, achieving up to 7.2 gains on LIBERO Long with only 0.31% / 3.87% additional parameters. Ablation studies validate the benefit of action-conditioned layer routing, while routing analyses reveal structured allocation patterns across action layers and task settings.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Planning Takes More Than Token Prediction: Causal Plan for Benchmarking and Building Physically Grounded Embodied Reasoners
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Zheng Lu, Mingqi Gao, Qinlei Xie, Wanqi Zhong, Hanwen Cui
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper introduces Causal-Plan-Bench and Causal Planner, emphasizing the need for physically grounded causal reasoning over token prediction in embodied vision-language planning.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Current benchmarks for embodied vision-language planning inadvertently favor linguistic next-token prediction over physically grounded next-state reasoning. This rewards models that mimic statistical language priors rather than track true causal dependencies, reducing complex physical planning to shallow sequence modeling. Hence, achieving genuine physical autonomy requires a fundamental shift from linguistically grounded token prediction toward physically grounded causal reasoning. To this end, we introduce Causal-Plan-Bench, a high-fidelity diagnostic suite spanning four causal dimensions, curated via multi-stage verification. To endow models with this capability, a four-stage annotation pipeline extracts structured interaction records from egocentric videos to construct Causal-Plan-1M, a dense million-scale corpus of explicit causal reasoning traces. Extensive evaluation reveals a striking gap: leading models struggle to demonstrate genuine physical agency -- even GPT-6-astra scores only 43.04. In contrast, our tailored training recipe enables Causal Planner to internalize the complex physical logic required for accurate next-state estimation. Built upon Qwen3-VL-8B, Causal Planner raises its backbone's score from 33.23 to 45.28, a 36.3% relative gain, and improves on three external benchmarks without benchmark-specific adaptation. We further observe an empirical Causal-Supervision Scaling Trend. Paired no-vision controls also reveal substantial visual dependence, while cross-judge comparisons and human scoring assess the reliability of automated evaluation. More importantly, we initiate the first effort to turn agents from superficial token predictors into physically grounded causal reasoners, bridging language modeling and world modeling.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Skin Tokens: A Learned Compact Representation for Unified Autoregressive Rigging
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Jia-peng Zhang, Cheng-Feng Pu, Meng-Hao Guo, Yan-Pei Cao, Shi-Min Hu
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper introduces SkinTokens, a learned representation for skinning weights that improves rigging accuracy and efficiency in 3D animation through a unified autoregressive framework.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: The rapid proliferation of generative 3D models has created a critical bottleneck in animation pipelines: rigging. Existing automated methods are fundamentally limited by their approach to skinning, treating it as an ill-posed, high-dimensional regression task that is inefficient to optimize and is typically decoupled from skeleton generation. We posit this is a representation problem and introduce SkinTokens: a learned, compact, and discrete representation for skinning weights. By leveraging an FSQ-CVAE to capture the intrinsic sparsity of skinning, we reframe the task from continuous regression to a more tractable token sequence prediction problem. This representation enables TokenRig, a unified autoregressive framework that models the entire rig as a single sequence of skeletal parameters and SkinTokens, learning the complicated dependencies between skeletons and skin deformations. The unified model is then amenable to a reinforcement learning stage, where tailored geometric and semantic rewards improve generalization to complex, out-of-distribution assets. Quantitatively, the SkinTokens representation leads to a 98%-133% percents improvement in skinning accuracy over state-of-the-art methods, while the full TokenRig framework, refined with RL, enhances bone prediction by 17%-22%. Our work presents a unified, generative approach to rigging that yields higher fidelity and robustness, offering a scalable solution to a long-standing challenge in 3D content creation.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Learning from Fleet Experience: A Collective Learning Paradigm for Robots
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Chao Yu, Shu'ang Yu, Hao Lin, Hongzhi Zang, Yuxiang Yan
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper presents a collective experience learning paradigm that enables robot fleets to enhance policy reliability by sharing execution experiences, achieving high success rates without needing additional expert corrections.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Experience generated during deployment offers an opportunity for robots to improve policy reliability through learning from their own executions. However, learning through human corrections requires teleoperators to monitor execution and intervene when policies fail, a demand that is difficult to meet as robot fleets grow. We introduce collective experience learning (CEL), a learning paradigm in which deployed robots share their execution experience to improve a common policy. We realize CEL through failure-guided experience retrieval fine-tuning (FERT), which uses failure contexts from robot executions to retrieve relevant trajectory segments from the fleet's shared successful experience and uses their actions as supervision for policy updates, without collecting additional expert demonstrations or corrective actions. A fault-tolerant asynchronous training system (FATS) coordinates experience collection, policy optimization and policy distribution despite local interruptions within the robot fleet. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, the resulting policies achieve success rates of 93.3-99.2%, evaluated over 120 trials per task on robots excluded from training data collection. With collection time per robot held fixed, larger fleets provide more experience and FERT generally achieves higher success rates across the evaluated sizes. On multi-stage phone packaging, learning with 96 robots increases success from 79.2% to 98.3%. These results support collective experience as a practical basis for scalable robot learning and a path towards improving policy reliability during deployment without collecting additional expert corrective actions.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: AeroDASH: Asynchronous Vision-Language-Action Control for Continuous UAV Flight
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Zhe Liu, Yuxuan Zheng, Jinzhe Qin, Ziqi Gao, Boyu Zhou
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: AeroDASH introduces an asynchronous vision-language-action framework for UAVs that enhances trajectory prediction accuracy and execution stability, achieving a 76.56% success rate in tests.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Onboard inference latency creates a mismatch between the trajectories predicted by vision-language-action (VLA) policies and the ongoing motion of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). We present AeroDASH, an asynchronous VLA framework for continuous language-conditioned flight. A B-spline policy is initialized through supervised fine-tuning on expert demonstrations, providing continuous trajectory references in position and yaw. During execution, trajectory fusion removes the expired prediction prefix and connects the remaining segment to the active reference with derivative continuity while limiting trajectory deformation. To account for deviations induced by asynchronous execution, execution-aware group relative policy optimization (GRPO) further adapts the policy using trajectory-level rewards. On the UAV-Flow test set, AeroDASH achieves a success rate of 76.56%, exceeding OpenVLA-UAV and AeroDASH w/o GRPO by 38.1 and 20.1 percentage points, respectively. Execution experiments show that AeroDASH sustains motion during inference and reduces acceleration, jerk, and speed fluctuations relative to asynchronous tracking of waypoint sequences. We further demonstrate language-conditioned flight with onboard inference and asynchronous trajectory execution. The code will be released upon acceptance.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: MMTA: Benchmarking Multimodal Temporal Analysis with Time Series, Text, and Vision
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Ziyang Zhang, Shenyi Li, Yilin Wang, Ziyun Cui, Bowen Zhou
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The MMTA benchmark evaluates multimodal temporal analysis across nine domains, revealing challenges in integrating time series with text and vision while introducing TimeOmni-v for improved model performance.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Time-series analysis is increasingly studied in multimodal settings, yet most benchmarks pair temporal signals with text or with visualizations derived from the same signal. This leaves open whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can integrate time series with real-world visual evidence. We introduce MMTA (multimodal temporal analysis), a benchmark of tri-modal tasks with diverse cross-modal complementarity patterns among time series, text, and vision. MMTA spans nine domains -- robotics, autonomous driving, human action, manufacturing, AR assistance, healthcare, recommendation, finance, and climate -- under video+TS and image+TS layouts, with a 3,524-sample test split covering classification and forecasting. The benchmark standardizes heterogeneous real-world sources into a shared schema with domain-specific prompts, provenance documentation, and success-weighted metrics that penalize both wrong answers and failed generations. Evaluating eight open-source and proprietary MLLMs reveals a shared bottleneck: representing time series as text creates very long token sequences and weakens fine-grained alignment with visual evidence, especially in long-video settings. We then introduce TimeOmni-v, a multimodal LLM extension with a dedicated time-series encoder, temporal positional alignment, modality-aware token layout, and a forecasting head. TimeOmni-v improves long-video classification and time-series inference efficiency, showing that MMTA not only exposes representation and grounding failures but also motivates targeted model design.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: BrandEval: A Two-Track Multi-Agent Benchmark for Risk-Sensitive LLM Crisis Communication
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Haotian Gan, Weidong Tang, Hanbin Sun, Yi Luo, Xintian Li
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: BrandEval introduces a two-track benchmark for evaluating LLMs in crisis communication, emphasizing dynamic stakeholder interactions and long-term risk management over static assessments.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Evaluating LLMs for crisis communication requires more than judging isolated responses, because public feedback and competitor actions can reshape trust over time. Existing benchmarks remain largely static and single-turn, offering limited evidence about long-horizon risk-sensitive communication. We introduce \textbf{BrandEval}, a two-track benchmark for product-crisis communication, focusing on public brand responses to product-related safety, quality, service, and trust incidents. BrandEval-Static evaluates stakeholder-aware strategic analysis, while BrandEval-Dynamic stress-tests response policies in \textbf{BrandPolis}, a controlled multi-agent sandbox with consumer feedback, competitor responses, and trust-risk trajectories. We also construct \textbf{BrandSRD}, a Chinese crisis-response dataset, and instantiate a reference Strategic Agent using \textbf{Strategic Rationale (SR)}. Across proprietary and open-source models, we find that static strategic quality is informative but incomplete: it aligns with some end-state outcomes but does not reliably predict volatility and delayed recovery; dynamic stress tests further expose tail-risk failures under manipulative or weakly grounded policies. The code and dataset will be available at https://github.com/htgan-ai/BrandEval.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Wen Xue, Yong Liu, Xueheng Li, Si Wu, Yong Xu
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: LayerEditor introduces a unified framework for high-quality image editing that generates reusable RGBA layers through instruction-guided editing and Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: High-quality image editing requires precise modification of target regions while preserving the content of unrelated regions. Existing editing models produce flattened outputs that limit precise local manipulation and layer reuse, while decomposition methods typically optimize layer recovery separately from instruction-driven editing. To this end, we introduce LayerEditor, a unified framework that couples instruction-guided image editing with controllable generation of reusable RGBA layers. At its core, In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling jointly represents the edited canvas and an ordered sequence of RGB-Alpha layers within a single token sequence, enabling semantic edits and explicit control over individual layer content. To retain the pretrained model's editing capability during adaptation to layered outputs, we propose Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation, which transfers its editing prior to both the edited canvas and the image composed from the predicted layers. To support training and evaluation, we construct LayerEditor-100K, a large-scale paired image-editing dataset with ordered RGBA layer annotations, and introduce dedicated benchmarks for layered editing. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LayerEditor maintains strong editing fidelity while generating accurate RGBA layers, supporting both flexible layer-level manipulation and multi-layer decomposition.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Empowering Edge Agents: A Systematic Analysis of Edge-Cloud Collaboration in LLM Agent Execution
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Pengcheng Huang, Zhenghao Liu, Shixin Ren, Shi Yu, Sijia Yao
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper presents EC2-Bench, a benchmark for analyzing edge-cloud collaboration in long-horizon LLM agent execution, revealing insights on performance, resource usage, and privacy dynamics.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Edge-cloud collaboration combines the lower inference overhead and greater data locality of edge-side execution with the stronger capabilities of cloud-hosted models. However, as LLM agents increasingly operate in long-horizon scenarios, cloud participation becomes interleaved throughout execution rather than a one-shot decision for each query. Such interleaved participation introduces trajectory-level effects that remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we introduce EC2-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating edge-cloud collaboration in long-horizon agent execution. It provides executable digital-workspace agent tasks and a unified evaluation framework covering task performance, resource usage, and privacy exposure. Using this benchmark, we empirically study diverse forms of edge-cloud collaboration. Our study reveals three findings. First, collaboration achieves a favorable balance among task performance, resource usage, and privacy exposure compared with edge-only and cloud-only execution. Second, as edge models become stronger, collaborative execution approaches cloud-only performance, and performance differences across strategies shrink, while privacy exposure remains strongly strategy-dependent. Third, stronger edge capability shifts preferred collaboration from externally controlled cloud participation and direct cloud execution toward more edge-controlled collaboration. Further analyses identify cloud-invocation decision-making and instruction following as important edge-side abilities for effective collaboration. These findings provide a systematic understanding of edge-cloud collaboration in long-horizon agent execution and insights for designing future edge agents that effectively collaborate with cloud models. Code and resources are available at https://github.com/OpenBMB/EC2-Bench.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: LPA-CWM: A Learned Physical Adjudicator for Motion Reasoning with Counterfactual World Models
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Kunwei Wu, Xiang Liu, Guocai Yao, Junming Chen, Zhikang Chen
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: LPA-CWM enhances motion reasoning by integrating physical priors into counterfactual world models, significantly improving motion correspondence metrics across various benchmarks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Counterfactual world models (CWM) extract motion from pretrained video predictors by comparing factual and intervened predictions, but uniform aggregation weights responses equally without explicitly incorporating physical priors. Our key insight is to incorporate physical priors into candidate reliability learning, motivating LPA-CWM with a lightweight Learned Physical Adjudicator (LPA). Trained on dense MOVi-F trajectories, the 3.0M-parameter LPA compares visual context and response structure across an unordered candidate set to predict relative weights; windowed localization and one paired re-evaluation recover motion with the CWM frozen. Existing video-level benchmarks do not directly assess motion correspondence, where low localization error can conceal missing trajectory segments. We introduce Completeness-aware Motion Correspondence (CMC), a ground-truth-anchored protocol jointly measuring localization, completeness, visibility, and continuity, counting missing predictions as failures on visible dynamic points. Across DAVIS, Kinetics, and RoboTAP, LPA-CWM improves all main CMC measures over Uniform CWM, with relative gains of 18.1%--60.0% in average Dynamic Correspondence Accuracy ($\mathrm{DCA}_{\mathrm{avg}}$), and improves TAP-Vid First tracking accuracy (overview: https://LPA-CWM.github.io).

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: ConfAL-WM: Confidence-Guided Active Learning for Action-Conditioned World Models
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Xiang Liu, Kunwei Wu, Miao Liu, Sen Cui, Changshui Zhang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: ConfAL-WM introduces a confidence-guided active learning framework to enhance action-conditioned world models by optimizing data allocation and training through localized confidence maps.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Action-conditioned world models have become an important foundation for embodied prediction, planning, and synthetic data generation, but their errors under new task and scene distributions are often concentrated in localized spatiotemporal regions such as robot arms, manipulated objects, contact areas, and occluded objects. This paper presents ConfAL-WM, a confidence-guided active learning framework for post-training embodied world models. Building upon EnerVerse-AC (EVAC), we attach a lightweight confidence probe to UNet decoder features and predict dense confidence maps in the latent space. These maps are aggregated into task-, frame-, and patch-level scores, enabling data-budget allocation and localized training enhancement. Our pipeline trains the probe and warms up EVAC on a small target-domain subset. EVAC-v1 then supplies task-level acquisition and optional frame/patch weighting signals; all selected-data models are initialized from the original pretrained EVAC checkpoint for retraining. Experiments on RoboTwin2.0 at the default 40% data budget show that confidence-guided selection improves post-training quality, while dense frame and patch weighting offers complementary reconstruction and semantic gains compared with scalar reward, progress, and judge-based scoring baselines. A quick visual overview of this work is available at https://ConfAL-WM.github.io.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: LIBERO-Pro2.0: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Robustness of Embodied Foundation Models
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Xueyang Zhou, Yangming Xu, Qianjiang Li, Guiyao Tie, Junhao Wu
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: LIBERO-Pro2.0 introduces a robust benchmark for evaluating embodied foundation models, revealing significant performance drops under diverse distribution shifts and emphasizing the need for systematic robustness assessment.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: LIBERO has emerged as a widely adopted benchmark for evaluating robotic manipulation policies. However, strong performance on LIBERO does not necessarily indicate robust embodied capabilities, as models may exploit benchmark-specific regularities rather than generalize to diverse operating conditions. In this work, we introduce LIBERO-Pro2.0, a comprehensive benchmark for systematically evaluating the robustness of embodied foundation models under distribution shifts. LIBERO-Pro2.0 encompasses 22 static perturbations and 20 runtime interventions across six dimensions: Condition, Environment, Observation, Execution, Robot State Configuration, and Language, yielding 1,648 validated shifted task instances. To support robustness-oriented learning, we further collect 39,390 training trajectories through model-generated and human demonstrations. All shifted task instances undergo six rounds of iterative human review and correction to ensure physical plausibility and task validity. We evaluate 17 representative robot policies spanning vision-language-action models, world-action models, and robustness-oriented policies. Our results reveal substantial robustness gaps across all evaluated paradigms: under runtime distribution shifts, the evaluated models exhibit an average performance drop of 26.5 percentage points, with individual drops reaching 32.5 points. These findings highlight the gap between nominal benchmark performance and robustness under distribution shifts, underscoring the need for systematic robustness evaluation of embodied foundation models.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Structured Latent Dynamics for Long-Horizon Embodied World Models
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Kevin Chen, Yu-Wei Zhan, Haoran Liang, Sen Cui, Changshui Zhang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper introduces HWM, a structured dynamics framework enhancing long-horizon predictions in embodied world models by stabilizing latent state evolution through Hamiltonian dynamics.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Reliable long-horizon prediction remains a central challenge for embodied world models. Although recent generative models can synthesize visually plausible action-conditioned futures, their latent dynamics are typically learned through unconstrained transition modules, which may gradually deviate from coherent physical evolution as predictions are recursively rolled forward. We investigate whether explicitly structuring latent state evolution can improve the stability and utility of such imagined trajectories. To this end, we introduce HWM, a structured dynamics framework that represents backbone latents in a learned phase space consisting of generalized coordinates and momenta. Future states are propagated through dissipative Hamiltonian dynamics and mapped back to the original latent representation through a learnable inverse interface. The resulting formulation can be integrated into existing world-model architectures without redesigning their perception or decoding components, while multi-step transition supervision encourages the structured rollout to remain aligned with the latent trajectories induced by real observations. Controlled simulation experiments show that HWM produces more accurate estimates of velocity, acceleration, and jerk and substantially reduces long-horizon energy drift relative to unstructured latent dynamics. We further evaluate the approach across three distinct embodied world-model settings, covering single-arm multi-view prediction with Ctrl-World, dual-arm single-view prediction with EVAC, and task-oriented single-arm prediction with Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B. On RoboCasa, incorporating HWM into Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B yields a 2.7% relative improvement in task success. On real-world AgiBot World trajectories, it improves nDTW by 9.7% with Ctrl-World and Logic by 8.4% with EVAC.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Shenyi Li, Ziyang Zhang, Wen Wu, Ming Liu, Chao Zhang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: Time-JEPA enhances video world models by incorporating temporally aligned physical time series as auxiliary supervision, improving predictions and understanding of physical interactions across multiple domains.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Video world models learn how visual environments evolve by predicting missing or future content. However, physical-state information can provide useful context for predicting how environments evolve. Prior work incorporates this information through different mechanisms: domain-specific physical laws can complicate multi-domain training, while supervision on individual frames or frame pairs gives limited attention to how physical state evolves over time. We introduce Time-JEPA, which fine-tunes a video world model using low-dimensional, temporally aligned physical time series as auxiliary supervision. Physical time series connect video representations with physical state at corresponding temporal positions, encouraging the model to preserve how physical state evolves. In multiple domains including autonomous driving, robot manipulation, and human motion, Time-JEPA improves current-state decoding, multi-horizon future-state prediction, and kinematic reconstruction over matched video-fine-tuned controls across both condition and state-variable distribution shifts. Multi-domain training provides aggregate gains over matched single-domain training in all three tasks. External evaluations further suggest that time-series supervision improves sensitivity to physical anomalies and the representation of physical interactions, including in unseen scenarios. Aggregate gains on a second video backbone indicate that the method can be applied to more backbones. These results suggest that physical time series help video world models better understand the physical world.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Learning When to Trust and Reobserve Sparse-Frame VideoQA from Temporal Sampling Perturbations
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Shujia Liu
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper presents PhaseGuard+, a method that enhances sparse-frame video-language models by predicting answer reliability and corrective actions based on temporal sampling perturbations.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Sparse-frame video-language models can change their answers when only the sampling timestamps shift. Raw agreement exposes this problem, but it need not rank errors better than token confidence or identify which additional observation will repair an answer. We argue that answer risk and action value must be estimated separately. PhaseGuard+ probes a frozen VLM at controlled temporal offsets, predicts the reliability of the phase-vote answer, and predicts the example-wise correctness gain of a specific rescue action. The second score routes only examples expected to benefit from denser frames or a stronger VLM. Both predictors use lightweight models trained on public data; the VLMs remain frozen. We use 256 Perception Test videos for method development and evaluate on a disjoint 256-video test set comprising 554 Physics questions. For Qwen3-VL-8B, reliability AUROC rises from 68.0% with token softmax to 74.8% (+6.8 pp, 95% CI [2.6, 10.7] pp). Routing 30% of questions to Qwen3-VL-32B reaches 67.87% accuracy, compared with 63.66% for budget-matched random routing (+4.21 percentage points, CI [1.89, 6.40]). All four tested rescue pairs significantly outperform random routing. Temporal sensitivity becomes actionable when the system learns both whether an answer is unreliable and whether an available action is likely to fix it.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: BFM-Zero: A Promptable Behavioral Foundation Model for Humanoid Control Using Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Yitang Li, Zhengyi Luo, Tonghe Zhang, Cunxi Dai, Anssi Kanervisto
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: BFM-Zero introduces a promptable behavioral foundation model for humanoid robots, enabling versatile control across tasks through a shared latent representation learned via unsupervised reinforcement learning.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Building Behavioral Foundation Models (BFMs) for humanoid robots has the potential to unify diverse control tasks under a single, promptable generalist policy. However, existing approaches are either exclusively deployed on simulated humanoid characters, or specialized to specific tasks such as tracking. We propose BFM-Zero, a framework that learns an effective shared latent representation that embeds motions, goals, and rewards into a common space, enabling a single policy to be prompted for multiple downstream tasks without retraining. This well-structured latent space in BFM-Zero enables versatile and robust whole-body skills on a Unitree G1 humanoid in the real world, via diverse inference methods, including zero-shot motion tracking, goal reaching, and reward optimization, and few-shot optimization-based adaptation. Unlike prior on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) frameworks, BFM-Zero builds upon recent advancements in unsupervised RL and Forward-Backward (FB) models, which offer an objective-centric, explainable, and smooth latent representation of whole-body motions. We further extend BFM-Zero with critical reward shaping, domain randomization, and history-dependent asymmetric learning to bridge the sim-to-real gap. Those key design choices are quantitatively ablated in simulation. A first-of-its-kind model, BFM-Zero establishes a step toward scalable, promptable behavioral foundation models for whole-body humanoid control.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Drive2Gauss: FeedForward 4D Gaussian Reconstruction from Multimodal Generative Driving Videos
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Tong Zhao, Zhiyuan Han, Lin Chen, Bowen Xie, Yunxi Qiao
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: Drive2Gauss introduces a feedforward framework for dynamic 4D Gaussian scene reconstruction from multimodal driving videos, enhancing efficiency and rendering capabilities without optimization.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Generating reusable driving environments requires both controllable future observations and an explicit representation that supports rendering from different viewpoints, yet existing methods still recover explicit scenes from generated RGB videos through optimization for each sequence. To overcome these limitations, we present Drive2Gauss, a feedforward framework that converts jointly generated RGB, metric depth, and dynamic flow into dynamic 4D Gaussian scenes. A Multimodal Video Generator predicts the three modalities from reference multiview images and future control signals. Furthermore, we introduce a Gaussian Query Decoder that uses depth to initialize sparse 3D queries and flow to associate the queries across time, and integrates appearance information through spatiotemporal feature aggregation and iterative query refinement. The reconstruction stage operates in a single feedforward pass without optimization for each scene. Extensive results on nuScenes demonstrate that our approach attains an FID of 6.38 and an FVD of 12.43 for future RGB generation, a PSNR of 29.91 dB when reconstructing its generated observations, and supports both direct rendering under lateral camera shifts and downstream video fixing. Code and more visualizations are available at https://zttt04. github.io/Drive2Gauss_page/.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: HAF-VLA: Hierarchical Action Flow Framework for Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Control
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Langzhe Gu, Chengkai Hou, Meng Li, Xinhua Wang, Xinyuan Lv
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: HAF-VLA is a hierarchical framework that enhances humanoid robots' vision-language-action control by progressively refining locomotion and manipulation actions through cross-stage conditioning.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Humanoid robots hold great promise as general-purpose agents in human-centered environments, yet adapting generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policies to real-world humanoid loco-manipulation remains challenging. Unlike fixed-base or wheeled manipulators, humanoids must coordinate locomotion, posture, gaze, and dual-arm manipulation over a high-dimensional whole-body action space, where inaccurate base or waist motions can easily induce unstable and aggressive upper-body compensation. We propose HAF-VLA, a hierarchical action-flow framework for humanoid VLA control. Built upon a pretrained flow-matching VLA, HAF-VLA inherits the vision-language prefix encoder and action expert weights, and adapts them to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation with learnable stage embeddings and cross-stage KV-cache conditioning. Instead of generating the full action chunk in a single pass, HAF-VLA progressively denoises a shared whole-body action space: first locomotion and head commands, then waist refinement, and finally full-body manipulation. To preserve structural dependencies across stages, we introduce a cross-stage KV cache conditioning mechanism, enabling subsequent action generation stages to refine and augment their outputs based on the action representations from preceding stages. Experimental results across six real-world tasks demonstrate that our framework significantly enhances the performance of existing models in humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, demonstrating an effective pathway for adapting strong mobile-manipulation VLAs to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: PrismWAM: Decoupling State Representations in World Action Models
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Tianyu Xin, Wanqi Zhong, Bowen Hu, Zhangchi Guo, Lijie Wang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: PrismWAM decouples semantic and physical state representations in World Action Models, enhancing manipulation performance by focusing on action-driven world evolution without extensive pretraining.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) typically represent the world through latent embeddings from pretrained video models, which entangle heterogeneous aspects of the world, from how it looks (e.g., texture and color) to how it is physically configured (e.g., occupancy and pose). This raises an underexplored question: $\textbf{what should constitute the state of a WAM?}$ We argue that the world state should separate how the world appears from how the world evolves under action: the former captures semantic context, while the latter is governed by physical state. To this end, we propose $\textbf{PrismWAM}$, which decouples physics from semantics while jointly modeling state and action. PrismWAM factorizes an embodied task into a $\mathrm{Semantic\ Planning}\rightarrow\mathrm{Physical\ Rollout}\rightarrow\mathrm{Executable\ Action}$ pipeline: given only the initial RGB observation, semantic planning learns to predict the final goal image, while physical rollout predicts the fine-grained evolution toward this goal in depth space; executable actions are then generated from the depth rollout. Without any embodied action pretraining or additional data augmentation, PrismWAM achieves strong manipulation performance in both simulation and the real world. Notably, PrismWAM even surpasses a broad range of models with large-scale embodied action pretraining (e.g., OpenWAM-$α$). More broadly, we reframe World Action Models from modeling how the world looks to how it responds to action, paving the way for action-centric world models grounded in occupancy, flow, tactile sensing, proprioception, and beyond.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: VeriCUA: Learning Proactive Verification for Reliable GUI Agent Rewards
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Zhizhou Wang, Yaxi Lu, Zhong Zhang, Zikun Hu, Xin Cong
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: VeriCUA introduces a proactive reward agent that optimizes verification strategies for GUI agents, significantly improving task success and efficiency over existing methods.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning for computer-use agents increasingly relies on proactive reward agents that interact with the post-execution GUI environment to verify what recorded screenshots cannot reveal. The reliability of such verification hinges on two coupled decisions: what to check and when to stop. Existing methods leave these decisions to prompted foundation models. However, neither scaling up the model nor providing few-shot examples reliably improves verification: prompted Judges ranging from 4B to GPT-5.4 all plateau at 68%-70% macro-average agreement. This is because the value of a check depends on the environment rather than the task alone, and becomes apparent only through execution. Learning from execution is itself constrained, as the Actor's terminal state cannot be faithfully replicated during training, allowing only one verification attempt per state. We introduce VeriCUA, a proactive reward agent that learns its verification strategy from these single attempts. A trainable Judge decides what to check and when to stop, while a frozen Probe executes the checks in the live environment. Online reinforcement learning optimizes the Judge for both verdict correctness and efficient Probe use, with returns normalized across terminal states. Trained only on OSWorld and evaluated without further training on MobileWorld and WebArena-Verified, VeriCUA achieves the highest reward agreement across all three benchmarks and lies on the agreement-cost Pareto frontier among proactive verifiers. It surpasses few-shot GPT-5.4 by 5.36 points with 47.6%-59.8% fewer Probe tokens, and even a 1B VeriCUA exceeds every prompted Judge. As the reward for Actor RL, it raises task success by 3.21 points overall and 5.40 points on held-out multi-application tasks. These results identify the verification strategy, not verifier scale, as the key to reliable GUI rewards.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: ActiveMem: Dynamic Latent Memory Trees for Long-Horizon Agents
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Song-Li Wu, Jingyi Wang, Zhaocheng Du, Weinan Gan
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: ActiveMem introduces a hierarchical memory framework that enhances long-horizon reasoning in agents by organizing experiences into dependency-aware trees, improving task completion and memory efficiency.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory to support long-horizon reasoning and decision making. Existing memory systems typically retrieve historical trajectories or summaries as independent context fragments, overlooking the procedural dependencies underlying multi-step execution. As memory scales, such flat retrieval introduces context fragmentation and cross-task interference, leading to structurally inconsistent reasoning trajectories. We propose ActiveMem, a hierarchical memory framework that recursively organizes agent experiences into dependency-aware latent execution trees. ActiveMem abstracts trajectories into reusable subtask nodes while explicitly preserving execution transitions, enabling coherent reasoning-path retrieval conditioned on the current execution state. To support continual adaptation, ActiveMem further learns dynamic memory expansion, retrieval, and pruning policies through reinforcement learning. Experiments across various agent benchmarks demonstrate that ActiveMem consistently improves task completion, reasoning stability, and memory efficiency over existing memory-based agents. Moreover, ActiveMem enables compact open-weight models to achieve competitive performance with substantially larger proprietary systems.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Humanoid Badminton: Learning Dynamic Racket Skills from Limited Human Motion Data
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Jingzhi Cui, Zhexiong Wang, Bangjie Xu, Pengyu Zhao, Youyuan Li
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: This paper presents a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework enabling humanoid robots to perform dynamic badminton skills and engage in multi-skill rallies with humans.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: High-speed racket sports provide a demanding testbed for humanoid robots, requiring time-critical decisions, precise striking, and dynamic whole-body coordination. In badminton, fast-changing shuttle trajectories require timely contact decisions, while successful returns demand precise racket pose and velocity within a brief contact window and across a broad three-dimensional striking workspace. Human motion data provide valuable priors for such athletic skills, but usable badminton references are limited and imperfect. Direct tracking provides insufficient executable variation for diverse shuttle conditions, while purely task-driven optimization may produce unnatural motion. We therefore present a three-stage hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for dynamic humanoid badminton. First, task-randomized motion augmentation expands sparse annotated hitting events into executable target-conditioned stroke variations, forming a continuous latent skill space. Second, a high-level planner outputs continuous latent skill codes to compose these skills online according to the observed shuttle state. Third, a context-conditioned adversarial regularizer encourages more natural planner-level skill usage while preserving return performance. In real-world deployment, our system sustains multi-skill rallies with human players, including forehand, backhand, and highly dynamic jump returns. This is the first real-world humanoid racket-sport system to demonstrate multi-skill human--robot rallies including highly dynamic jump returns.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: When Seeing Is Not Believing -- A Benchmark for Search-Grounded Video Misinformation Detection
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Tao Yu, Yujia Yang, Shenghua Chai, Jinshuai Zhang, Haopeng Jin
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The paper presents EVID-Bench, a benchmark for detecting video misinformation through cross-video comparison, revealing significant challenges in current multimodal models' accuracy.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Video misinformation increasingly operates at the semantic and evidential level: authentic footage may be selectively edited, temporally reordered, spliced across sources, or augmented with AI-generated content to construct false narratives. Such evidence-dependent manipulations cannot be reliably verified from the input video alone, because the missing, reordered, replaced, or recontextualized evidence lies outside the video itself. We introduce \textbf{EVID-Bench}, a benchmark for search-grounded video misinformation detection, where a system must search the open web for related videos and identify what information is false through cross-video comparison. EVID-Bench comprises 222 videos spanning 9 manipulation types across 3 categories: AI generation, single-source editing, and multi-source editing. All samples are verified to be undetectable by frontier models through visual inspection alone. We evaluate nine frontier multimodal models using a retrieval-augmented verification baseline. The best system achieves only 61.43\% point-level accuracy and 43.24\% video-level accuracy, while AI-generated manipulations remain especially challenging. Error analysis reveals recurring challenges: models fixate on irrelevant anchors, misattribute synthetic content to editorial splicing, and terminate search prematurely before fully explaining the manipulation.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: ELAN4D: Embodiment-Centric 4D Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models via Plug-and-Play Adaptation
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Zeyuan He, Bowen Yang, Zhirui Fang, Keru Zhou, Lei Jiang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: ELAN4D enhances Vision-Language-Action models by integrating 4D predictive supervision from robot keypoint tracks, improving robustness and generalization in robotic manipulation tasks.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promise for robotic manipulation, yet most existing policies operate reactively by directly regressing actions from current observations, without explicitly modeling future dynamics. This limits their ability to generalize under out-of-distribution perturbations. To address this issue, we propose ELAN4D, an embodiment-centric, 4D-aware training framework that enhances VLA policies with future robot keypoint tracks as predictive spatio-temporal supervision. Using only forward kinematics from proprioceptive states, we derive 3D displacement tracks of robot keypoints, such as joints and the end-effector, with negligible preprocess cost. These tracks provide metric and compact supervision without requiring external trackers or reconstruction. A plug-and-play auxiliary branch with a lightweight track decoder injects this 4D signal into the action expert while preserving the pretrained vision-language backbone through gradient isolation. The track decoder is discarded during inference, leaving the base policy interface unchanged. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0 and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that ELAN4D consistently improves over strong VLA baselines, achieving the best overall performance and substantial gains under out-of-distribution perturbations, including camera, background, and layout shifts. These results highlight the effectiveness of embodiment-centric 4D supervision for building more robust and generalizable manipulation policies.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Benchmarking the Limits of In-Context Reinforcement Learning for Ad-Hoc Teamwork
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Yuheng Jing, Kai Li, Ziwen Zhang, Jiajun Zhang, Zeyao Ma
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The paper introduces the ICRL4AHT benchmark to evaluate In-Context Reinforcement Learning's limitations in Ad-Hoc Teamwork, revealing poor adaptation in multi-agent scenarios despite success in single-agent tasks.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: In-Context Reinforcement Learning (ICRL) has enabled foundation agents to adapt instantaneously to novel tasks, yet its efficacy in Ad-Hoc Teamwork (AHT)-where coordination with unknown partners is required-remains unexplored. To rigorously evaluate this, we introduce a large-scale benchmark ICRL4AHT, built upon a high-throughput JAX implementation of Overcooked-V2. Our benchmark includes a large, diverse teammate suite spanning both RL and heuristic policies, enabling controlled train-test shifts, and provides a reproducible end-to-end pipeline for teammate generation, learning-history collection, dataset construction, and online multi-episode evaluation. We evaluate representative history-conditioned ICRL algorithms, including Algorithm Distillation (AD) and Decision-Pretrained Transformer (DPT), across millions of transitions. Results reveal notable limitations: contrary to their success in single-agent domains, these baselines fail to exhibit robust test-time adaptation in multi-agent settings. Specifically, these methods frequently underperform random baselines across both unseen teammate and unseen layout tracks, with no clear in-context improvement over long horizons. These findings highlight the challenges of strategic inference under partial observability within the OvercookedV2 AHT protocol, establishing our benchmark as a critical testbed for next-generation coordination algorithms.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: MVISTA-4D: View-Consistent 4D World Model with Test-Time Action Inference for Robotic Manipulation
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Jiaxu Wang, Yicheng Jiang, Tianlun He, Jingkai Sun, Qiang Zhang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: MVISTA-4D introduces a view-consistent 4D world model for robotic manipulation, enabling comprehensive scene dynamics prediction and optimized action inference from single-view RGBD inputs.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: World-model-based imagine-then-act becomes a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, yet existing approaches typically support either purely image-based forecasting or reasoning over partial 3D geometry, limiting their ability to predict complete 4D scene dynamics. This work proposes a novel embodied 4D world model that enables geometrically consistent, arbitrary-view RGBD generation: given only a single-view RGBD observation as input, the model imagines the remaining viewpoints, which can then be back-projected and fused to assemble a more complete 3D structure across time. To efficiently learn the multi-view, cross-modality generation, we explicitly design cross-view and cross-modality feature fusion that jointly encourage consistency between RGB and depth and enforce geometric alignment across views. Beyond prediction, converting generated futures into actions is often handled by inverse dynamics, which is ill-posed because multiple actions can explain the same transition. We address this with a test-time action optimization strategy that backpropagates through the generative model to infer a trajectory-level latent best matching the predicted future, and a residual inverse dynamics model that turns this trajectory prior into accurate executable actions. Experiments on three datasets demonstrate strong performance on both 4D scene generation and downstream manipulation, and ablations provide practical insights into the key design choices.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Junxi Wang, Te Sun, Jiayi Zhu, Chen Zhang, Siyuan Li
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: MemForest is a memory compression framework that efficiently partitions and merges agent memory, achieving significant storage reduction and retrieval speedup while maintaining high performance.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Agent memory systems have demonstrated significant potential in long-term dialogue, personalized assistants, and video understanding. However, continuously accumulated memory introduces substantial storage and retrieval costs during inference. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{MemForest}, a general memory compression framework adaptable to various agent memory systems. Specifically, MemForest partitions historical memory into event-centric units by leveraging global semantic similarity and local temporal continuity. For each unit, it constructs a maximum spanning tree, termed an EventTree, and progressively merges redundant memory nodes by selecting high-weight edges, reducing storage overhead. Furthermore, we introduce an anchor-guided propagation retrieval mechanism that retrieves relevant memory nodes from the temporal neighborhoods of key nodes, improving retrieval accuracy. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of MemForest. Under the unimodal Mem0 framework, MemForest retains \textbf{97.1%} of the original performance while compressing \textbf{50%} of historical memory across three benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and PersonaMem), achieving a \textbf{1.89x} retrieval speedup. Under the multimodal M3-Agent framework, it preserves \textbf{99.7%} of the original performance with a \textbf{50%} compression ratio across two benchmarks (M3-Bench-robot and M3-Bench-web), achieving a \textbf{2.24x} retrieval speedup. \textcolor{RoyalBlue}{\textit{Our code is available at [https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}}](https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}})

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Latent-WAM: Latent World Action Modeling for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Linbo Wang, Yupeng Zheng, Qiang Chen, Shiwei Li, Yichen Zhang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: Latent-WAM introduces a novel autonomous driving framework utilizing spatially-aware latent representations for improved trajectory planning, achieving state-of-the-art results with fewer resources.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: We introduce Latent-WAM, an efficient end-to-end autonomous driving framework that achieves strong trajectory planning through spatially-aware and dynamics-informed latent world representations. Existing world-model-based planners suffer from inadequately compressed representations, limited spatial understanding, and underutilized temporal dynamics, resulting in sub-optimal planning under constrained data and compute budgets. Latent-WAM addresses these limitations with two core modules: a Spatial-Aware Compressive World Encoder (SCWE) that distills geometric knowledge from a foundation model and compresses multi-view images into compact scene tokens via learnable queries, and a Dynamic Latent World Model (DLWM) that employs a causal Transformer to autoregressively predict future world status conditioned on historical visual and ego status representations. Extensive experiments on NAVSIM v2 and HUGSIM demonstrate new state-of-the-art results: 89.3 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 and 28.9 HD-Score on HUGSIM, surpassing the best prior perception-free method by 3.2 EPDMS with significantly less training data and a compact 104M-parameter model. The code and model weights have been open-sourced at https://github.com/yukki555/Latent-WAM.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: GazeAgent: VLM-Guided Implicit Gaze Calibration from Egocentric Multimodal Behavior for AI Glasses
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Yuhong Zhang, Khanh An Nguyen, Xinyu Tian, KungYi Chang, Abraham Padua
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: GazeAgent is a VLM-guided framework that enhances gaze calibration in AI glasses by adaptively utilizing multimodal behavior without user interruption, significantly improving accuracy.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: AI glasses typically require explicit, user-specific eye-tracker calibration, and accuracy can drift when the device shifts during use. We present GazeAgent, a VLM-guided framework that continuously and adaptively improves gaze-calibration accuracy from naturally occurring behavior without asking users to interrupt their activities. GazeAgent identifies precise visual attention (PVA) events from multimodal streams of inertial measurement unit (IMU), gaze, and wearer-hand signals, validates their task relevance, and localizes functional targets as pseudo-calibration targets. In a 10-participant scripted study, the system detected all 820 predefined PVA opportunities and, under device disturbance, reduced median gaze error by 44.1% compared with explicit calibration. In a five-participant case study, autonomous calibration produced the lowest workload and interruption ratings, and all participants preferred it for routine use. By deriving task-critical targets from natural multimodal behavior, GazeAgent demonstrates the potential for continuous, adaptive, and low-burden gaze interaction on egocentric AI glasses.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Tianqi Liu, Hanfei Zhao, Qifeng Liang, Hui En Pang, Jiarui Xu
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: Ropedia W0 introduces a unified loco-manipulation world model leveraging extensive egocentric data to enhance performance across diverse human and robotic embodiments in real-time interactions.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specific forward kinematics with extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. We also introduce Xp-Teleop, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data. Evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across five cross-embodiment benchmarks (DreamDojo, $Ψ_0$, $ω$-HOME, Xp-Teleop, and AgiBot) and on held-out human egocentric video, from zero-shot inference to few-shot and full-data post-training. Scaling human pre-training data improves performance on both human and robot evaluations. After distillation, our model supports real-time, minute-long rollouts, enabling live VR interaction. Applications in policy evaluation, model-based planning, and world-action modeling further demonstrate the model's utility for embodied decision-making.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: GPT-6 Astra Is a Native Visuo-Tactile Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Chen Yang, Linzhe Shi, Hang Zhang, Mu Xu, Jiansheng Fan
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: GPT-6 Astra demonstrates effective visuo-tactile manipulation by interpreting tactile images for contact-rich tasks, outperforming specialist policies and suggesting potential for joint visual-tactile pretraining.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Recent advances in multimodal models have enabled GPT-6 Astra to perform robotic manipulation through in-context learning. Yet contact-rich control and tactile perception are often regarded as strengths of specialist policies, leaving open whether Astra can directly understand and use tactile observations. We provide, to our knowledge, the first demonstration that Astra directly interprets vision-based tactile images and uses their contact cues for manipulation. Tactile RGB images enter through its existing visual interface, enabling few-shot closed-loop control on nineteen simulated UniVTAC and OpenViTac tasks with 210 sampled scene seeds per setting. With visuo-tactile input, Astra achieves mean success rates of 93.8% and 81.8%, exceeding the strongest reported specialist baselines in our comparison by 22.9 and 13.1 percentage points, respectively. Vision-only performance also leads these baselines, reaching 76.3% and 80.6%. Trajectory analysis reveals active probing, cautious grasping, contact-guided alignment, and recovery, alongside difficulties with tangential loading and corrective execution. Our findings challenge the exclusivity of specialist policies in contact-rich manipulation and show that fine-grained vision can partially compensate for missing touch. They also identify vision-based tactile sensing as an interface for scaling contact understanding with foundation models and reveal signs of benchmark saturation. These results motivate joint visual-tactile pretraining, harder contact-rich evaluations, and physical-robot validation.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: State World Models: Execute the Rules, Generate the Pixels
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Chan Yan Ki, Yanran Zhang, Wenzhao Zheng, Xiaofeng Wang, Zheng Zhu
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The Stateful Harness framework enhances world models by decoupling state evolution from video rendering, enabling rule-governed interactions that effectively handle hidden states.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Existing world models can generate action-conditioned video from a single image. Many focus on camera movement, allowing users to explore the generated scene. However, navigation alone does not ensure that an action follows persistent rules when its outcome depends on state that is invisible in the current frame. We present Stateful Harness, a framework that separates world evolution from video rendering to support stateful and rule-governed interaction. It maintains an evolving world state under specified rules, renders each resulting event with a frozen video model, and uses the generated clip to update the world state for the next turn. At each turn, the harness resolves the action selected by the user and compiles the resulting event into an instruction, while a preview clip from an editable 3D scene provides spatial and camera guidance. To evaluate rule compliance, we build WorldState-Bench, a benchmark of 50 counterfactual twin pairs that share an initial frame and action but differ in hidden state and required outcome. Under rule-only prompting, the best of the 11 evaluated video backends produces the required endings for both cases in 32% of pairs. For MiniMax-H3, specifying the required endings raises this rate from 32% to 64%, while the full harness reaches 92% with the same frozen model. These results support separating rule execution from video rendering for world interactions with hidden state.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: V-JEPA Hand: Simple, Accurate and Fast 3D Hand and Camera Trajectory Recovery from Egocentric Videos
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Ruicheng Li, Qixiu Li, Yu Deng, Sicheng Xu, Jiaolong Yang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: V-JEPA Hand is a fast, accurate model that jointly recovers 3D hand and camera trajectories from egocentric videos using a self-supervised approach.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Egocentric video supports diverse applications, including robot learning, augmented reality, and human activity understanding. Recovering metric 3D hand trajectories from such video requires estimating both hand motion and camera egomotion to express the hands in a consistent reference frame. Many existing pipelines recover hand and camera motion in separate stages, combining hand detection, hand reconstruction, camera tracking, and trajectory refinement. We present V-JEPA Hand, a simple feed-forward video model that jointly reconstructs bilateral hand motion and camera motion from egocentric clips. It uses a self-supervised V-JEPA 2.1 encoder to extract spatio-temporal features from full-frame video and a query-based predictor to decode these features into per-frame hand poses, hand presence, and camera motion. We use the predicted camera motion to express the hand trajectories in a common world frame. The model accepts known focal lengths or predicts them when unavailable. It reconstructs each clip in a single forward pass. We train both components end to end in a single stage on a mixture of diverse pseudo-labelled videos and high-precision 3D annotations. A single model achieves the lowest coverage-aware mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) among comparable baselines on ARCTIC, HOT3D, and EgoStandard. It also yields lower world-frame trajectory errors than the compared SLAM-based pipelines. Ablations support the benefits of video pretraining, temporal context, and mixed supervision. V-JEPA Hand achieves a forward-pass throughput of 93.4 FPS on a single RTX A6000. Project page: https://qft-333.github.io/V-JEPA-Hand-Page/.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: HandsOn: A Large-Scale Simulation Benchmark for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Tianwei Luo, Yiming He, Hongjin Wu, Ting Pan, Debin Ren
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: HandsOn is a comprehensive simulation benchmark for dexterous manipulation, featuring diverse robotic platforms and tasks to evaluate generalization and sim-to-real transfer in manipulation skills.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: General-purpose manipulation requires reliable behavior across embodiments, objects, and task demands. We introduce HandsOn, a composable simulation platform and benchmark for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation. It supports five robotic arms, six dexterous hands, and approximately 200 rigid, articulated, and deformable assets in randomized scenes. The benchmark pairs 18,000 curated human demonstrations with 66 human-verified tasks: Core-50 supports demonstration-based learning and execution tests, while Transfer-16 evaluates asset and relation transfer, skill composition, and deformable manipulation without target-task training demonstrations. Qualitative real-robot rollouts illustrate sim-to-real transfer. Across diffusion, vision-language-action, world-action, and prompted VLM-based methods, the best trained multi-task policy achieves 29.1% Core-50 success. Without benchmark finetuning, GPT-6 using move_eef for palm-and-finger control achieves 5.2% on Core-50 and 1.9% on Transfer-16 over 660 trials. Trained-policy stage diagnostics expose failures in contact establishment, action coordination, and maintaining achieved goals, with additional sequencing errors in composed tasks. HandsOn provides a shared basis for investigating manipulation generalization and the limits of reliable physical interaction.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Xinhao Ji, Hui En Pang, Hao Li, Kairui Hu, Jiner Wang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: EgoXperience introduces a comprehensive framework for learning coherent egocentric representations from video, achieving significant improvements in joint reconstruction and object pose estimation.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Reconstructing human activity from egocentric video requires more than recovering individual 3D components: the observer's motion, surrounding geometry, and hand-object interactions must fit together in a consistent world. Achieving this coherence requires both joint reconstruction and aligned supervision, yet existing methods and datasets offer limited support for either. We present EgoXperience, a full-stack paradigm that addresses these needs through data collection, automatic annotation, unified modeling, and benchmarking. Central to EgoXperience is an automatic annotation engine, EgoX-Engine, that couples geometrically verified object tracking with SLAM-based world alignment, yielding consistent supervision for the camera, scene, hands, and objects. This yields EgoX-Data-6M, a 50-hour dataset of task-driven manipulation and locomotion within and across indoor and outdoor environments, with second-level task captions. We carefully select one hour across these activity categories as EgoX-Bench to evaluate joint reconstruction. To translate this supervision into reconstruction, we introduce EgoX, trained with EgoX-Data-6M and complementary annotations from additional public datasets. Given monocular egocentric video and first-frame object masks, our model achieves joint metric reconstruction of the camera, scene, hands, and objects in a shared world coordinate frame with a single forward pass. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across scene estimation and world-space hand-object pose recovery. Against the strongest evaluated baselines, EgoX reduces camera, hand, and depth errors by 68.9%, 65.6%, and 42.9%, and improves object pose scores by 28.0%.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Robotic Photography System based on Vision-Language-Action Model
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Song-Li Wu, Chubin Zhang, Wenbo Ding, Yansong Tang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: RoboPhoto-VLA is a unified framework for robotic photography that integrates perception, reasoning, and camera control to produce aesthetically pleasing images aligned with human preferences.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Modern robotic photography requires understanding photographic intent, planning camera motions, and producing aesthetically pleasing images in complex environments. We present RoboPhoto-VLA, a unified Vision-Language-Action framework that jointly models perception, reasoning, and camera control for autonomous robotic photography. RoboPhoto-VLA incorporates PhotoCoT for structured action planning and Aesthetic Direct Preference Optimization (ADPO) to align camera behaviors with human aesthetic preferences. To facilitate training and evaluation, we construct OpenPhotography, a robotic photography dataset with language-guided demonstrations. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that RoboPhoto-VLA produces photographs better aligned with human aesthetic preferences while generalizing effectively to unseen subjects, viewpoints, poses, and complex photographic instructions.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: UniW(A)M: A Unified Mixture-of-Experts Framework for World and World-Action Models
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Jingbo Xu, Jianjie Fang, Zhuohang Li, Zihao Song, Zhaolu Wang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: UniW(A)M is a unified framework that integrates world and world-action models using diffusion Transformers, enhancing prediction and control efficiency in robotic tasks.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: World models (WMs) and world-action models (WAMs) focus on future world prediction and executable action generation, respectively. Although these models learn shared physical dynamics and interaction semantics from embodied trajectories, they are typically trained in isolation, which restricts knowledge reuse between prediction and control. The central challenge is therefore to develop a unified learning framework that shares these dynamics while preserving the distinct modeling capabilities required by each paradigm. We propose UniW(A)M, a mixture-of-experts world-(action) model built upon diffusion Transformers that unifies action-conditioned world modeling and diverse WAM variants. Shared experts capture common dynamics, while atomic capability experts are reused across interfaces so that each interface keeps its own conditional pathway. At deployment, a plug-in adaptive interface router (PAIR) learns from a small subset of target-task chunk scenarios to select a suitable WAM interface for each execution chunk, balancing task success and execution efficiency while keeping the backbone frozen. We evaluate UniW(A)M on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and three real-world manipulation tasks, where it achieves 88.3% average real-world success versus 76.7% for the strongest baseline. On WorldArena, it leads action-conditioned world modeling on all three tasks. AC-WM co-training contributes to action generation on every action interface and PAIR raises OOD success from 63.3% to 76.7%.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: LayerRoute: Action-Conditioned Mixture-of-Layers Routing for Vision-Language-Action Policies
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Zheng Lu, Haoran Liao, Wanqi Zhong, Yunhe Ni, Lijie Wang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: LayerRoute enhances Vision-Language-Action policies by enabling adaptive routing of visual-semantic representations and action states, improving performance with minimal parameter increase.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies leverage pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to guide action generation for robot control. VLMs provide hierarchical visual-semantic representations that evolve across layers, from local visual geometry to abstract, language-aligned semantics; different manipulation tasks may therefore require different mixtures of layer representations. Meanwhile, the action module maintains intermediate representations that evolve throughout action computation and may provide useful information for subsequent decisions.
