情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Dense temporal audio-visual captioning is important for multimodal video understanding and generation. However, prior work is constrained by three main limitations: (1) the lack of a dataset combining high temporal resolution, longer videos, and bidirectional alignment between time and events; (2) the reliance of most existing RL methods on checklists; and (3) the lack of a benchmark that bidirectionally evaluates event semantic correctness and temporal accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose: (1) AVTime-50K, a high-quality 50K-scale dataset with temporally precise, semantically accurate captions and longer videos; (2) AVTime, a state-of-the-art model optimized with a novel Bidirectional Temporal-Semantic Alignment (BiTSA) reward that imposes explicit bidirectional constraints between time and events; and (3) AVTime-Bench, a specialized benchmark that introduces a novel bidirectional evaluation of temporal accuracy and semantic correctness. Our code, models, and datasets are available at https://huggingface.co/collections/Apryle/avtime.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: TESS: LLM-guided Translation, Exploration, Simulation, and Search for Embodied Task Planning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Peiran Xu, Yixiang Yang, Jinghan Li, Fei Li, Cao Sheng
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents TESS, an LLM-guided search algorithm that enhances embodied task planning by integrating commonsense knowledge for efficient exploration and action selection in complex environments.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: In this work we focus on the problem of embodied task planning, which requires an agent to accomplish a complex task by separating it into atomic actions. Recent studies have developed LLM-based methods to address this problem. However, the executability and correctness of the generated plans remain suboptimal in complex environments and tasks. On the other hand, classical search algorithms have the potential to solve the planning problems perfectly, yet they require fully observable environments, known state transitions and goal state, which are often unattainable in general task domains. Therefore, we propose to implement an LLM-guided search algorithm that makes the search process possible and efficient by incorporating LLMs' commonsense knowledge. Our method leverages LLMs to (1) translate natural language instructions into formatted goal conditions, (2) facilitate efficient exploration in partially observable environments, (3) implement a rule-based world simulator, and (4) prune the space of candidate actions to improve search efficiency. Experimental results on VirtualHome and ALFWorld demonstrate its superior performance.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: CoEvolve: Self-Evolving Code Policies from Skills to Strategies for Humanoid Robots
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zicheng Liu, Haochen Wu, Jiawei He, Suyun Zhao, Huan Yang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: CoEvolve is a framework enabling humanoid robots to adaptively coordinate through executable code, enhancing multi-robot collaboration in complex tasks despite physical execution deviations.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Recent advances in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and World Action Models (WAMs) have expanded the manipulation and whole body capabilities of individual robots. Yet a single robot remains limited by its embodiment, and many real world tasks require capabilities that can only emerge through cooperation. Existing multi robot frameworks largely emphasize task decomposition, allocation, and replanning, while providing limited support for adapting executable coordination when physical execution deviates from the intended behavior. We present CoEvolve, a framework that represents team coordination as executable code over fixed robot motor skills. CoEvolve introduces Verifier Guided Coordination Evolution, where a multimodal foundation model instantiates coordination strategies through motion primitives, semantic objectives, temporary robot roles, and bounded execution parameters. Physical verification evaluates each executed transition, rejected behaviors trigger structured coordination revision from an accepted checkpoint, and verified experience is retained to guide subsequent decisions. We evaluate CoEvolve with two simulated Unitree G1 humanoids transporting a freely supported rigid payload through constrained corridors. Across 15 base task runs with three multimodal backbone families, CoEvolve completes 8 tasks, with every backbone achieving end to end success. Additional evaluations yield verified placement on two additional corridor layouts and after both same-backbone and cross-backbone experience initialization, while exposing persistent limitations in motion precision and contact stability. These results support executable coordination as a practical interface for adapting long horizon multi robot collaboration under shared physical constraints.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiadi You, Qize Yu, Yue Chen, Minghong Cai, Zhide Zhong
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: AffordanceWAM is a generative model that enhances robot manipulation by integrating affordance-aware predictions from diverse human videos and robot actions for improved interaction and performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Generalizable robot manipulation requires predicting how a scene will evolve, identifying where interactions are feasible, and determining how to act. Action-labeled robot videos directly supervise control but are costly and limited in diversity, whereas egocentric human videos capture diverse interactions but lack robot actions and differ in embodiment and appearance. We introduce AffordanceWAM, an affordance-aware generative World Action Model that represents object-centric spatiotemporal affordance through Scalar Affordance and Affordance Heatmap, within the generated future World. This representation grounds visual prediction in task-relevantant objects and interaction regions for action generation, and provides shared interaction targets across human and robot videos. Built on a pretrained video diffusion Transformer, AffordanceWAM uses separately parameterized World and Action Experts, coupled through Masked Joint Self-Attention, to jointly predict future RGB observations, Scalar Affordance fields, Affordance Heatmaps, and continuous robot actions under a unified flow-matching objective. Human videos supervise all three future-World streams, whereas robot trajectories additionally provide action supervision, enabling transfer without human action labels or retargeting. Experiments on RoboCasa, CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D, and real-world manipulation demonstrate consistent gains over RGB-only and robot-data-only baselines. Under fixed robot supervision, RoboCasa performance improves monotonically as affordance-annotated human video scales. These results support affordance as an effective interface for both vision-language-action learning and human-to-robot transfer.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Beyond Explicit Intent: Discovering and Shaping Artistic Intent through Human-AI Co-Creation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Renye Yan, Jialun Zhong, Jikang Cheng, Yi Gao, Yanzeng Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents a human-AI co-creation framework that enhances artistic intent discovery and shaping by allowing artists to explore and refine preferences through interaction with generative AI.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Generative AI is becoming an important medium for artistic creation, yet existing interactions often assume that creators can specify intentions in advance and accurately communicate them through text prompts. Artistic intentions, however, may be vague, latent, or recognizable only after seeing concrete visual possibilities. We propose a human-AI co-creation paradigm beyond explicit intent expression. By expanding model exploration, we expose artists to diverse visual possibilities, allowing them to identify previously unarticulated preferences through observation, comparison, and selection. We then integrate artists' curatorial judgments into reinforcement learning, assigning different learning strengths based on preferences over generation trajectories, so recognized directions are more strongly reinforced and the model gradually adapts to individual aesthetics. This creates a continuous "explore-identify-shape-re-explore" loop in which artistic intent is progressively discovered, externalized, and shaped. Through three user studies, we examine latent-preference discovery, personalized preference alignment, and the externalization of vague, difficult-to-express creative intentions.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: RL Teaches VLMs Where to Attend but Not How to Perceive
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Ziqian Zhang, Junjie Liao, Zhining Zhang, Wentao Zhu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Reinforcement learning enhances Vision-Language Models' task success by improving attention to visual information, but does not significantly boost their grounded visual understanding capabilities.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Although reinforcement learning (RL) effectively trains Vision-Language Model (VLM) agents, the mechanisms behind these capability gains are poorly understood. Across four diverse agent environments, we investigate whether the task-success gains from multi-turn RL are accompanied by improved grounded visual question answering about the environment. To assess this, we design environment-specific grounded VQA tasks that reveal improvements in grounded visual understanding. Representational probing shows that vision-encoder probe accuracy remains relatively stable, while LLM-layer probe accuracy improves. Attention analysis further reveals that LLM layers pay more attention to visual tokens during RL training. To test whether increased attention to visual tokens contributes to VQA gains, we introduce a lightweight plug-and-play intervention using a fixed attention bias. Without updating model parameters or computing gradients, this intervention partially restores VQA gains on the untrained model. These results reveal better utilization of visual information as a key mechanism behind the gains from RL.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: HAF-VLA: Hierarchical Action Flow Framework for Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Control
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Langzhe Gu, Chengkai Hou, Meng Li, Xinhua Wang, Xinyuan Lv
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: HAF-VLA is a hierarchical framework that enhances humanoid robots' vision-language-action control by progressively refining locomotion and manipulation actions through cross-stage conditioning.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Humanoid robots hold great promise as general-purpose agents in human-centered environments, yet adapting generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policies to real-world humanoid loco-manipulation remains challenging. Unlike fixed-base or wheeled manipulators, humanoids must coordinate locomotion, posture, gaze, and dual-arm manipulation over a high-dimensional whole-body action space, where inaccurate base or waist motions can easily induce unstable and aggressive upper-body compensation. We propose HAF-VLA, a hierarchical action-flow framework for humanoid VLA control. Built upon a pretrained flow-matching VLA, HAF-VLA inherits the vision-language prefix encoder and action expert weights, and adapts them to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation with learnable stage embeddings and cross-stage KV-cache conditioning. Instead of generating the full action chunk in a single pass, HAF-VLA progressively denoises a shared whole-body action space: first locomotion and head commands, then waist refinement, and finally full-body manipulation. To preserve structural dependencies across stages, we introduce a cross-stage KV cache conditioning mechanism, enabling subsequent action generation stages to refine and augment their outputs based on the action representations from preceding stages. Experimental results across six real-world tasks demonstrate that our framework significantly enhances the performance of existing models in humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, demonstrating an effective pathway for adapting strong mobile-manipulation VLAs to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: RIFAR: Reliability-Informed and Forgetting-Aware Replay for Continual Robot Learning with World-Action Models
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Tu Lin, Zheng Lu, Zirui Song, Zixian Lin, Zebang Feng
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: RIFAR enhances continual robot learning by using reliability-informed generative replay to efficiently adapt to new tasks while minimizing catastrophic forgetting and action drift.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Genuine embodied agency requires robots to turn continuous real-world experience into lasting, transferable skills. This demands continual learning that integrates new capabilities while preserving prior knowledge in evolving environments. Experience replay mitigates catastrophic forgetting, but storing complete demonstrations becomes costly as tasks accumulate. World-action models provide an alternative through generative replay. However, visually coherent rollouts may contain actions that cannot realize the predicted transitions, while new-task adaptation can disrupt learned behavior. To address these problems, we propose RIFAR (Reliability-Informed and Forgetting-Aware Replay), a reliability-informed and drift-aware generative replay framework. It reconstructs trajectories from compact historical demonstration prefixes and uses a trainable inverse-dynamics model to assess action-visual consistency. It first adapts to new tasks using current-task demonstrations and high-reliability replay, then evaluates how this adaptation changes action predictions on historical inputs and prioritizes reliable trajectories with greater action drift for further training. Across three LIBERO suites and real-world experiments, RIFAR outperforms the previous state of the art in WAM-based generative replay. On LIBERO-Goal, it achieves an AUC of 90.97 while retaining only 320 historical time steps per task, about 4.9% of those retained by 50-demonstration replay.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: When Seeing Is Not Believing -- A Benchmark for Search-Grounded Video Misinformation Detection
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Tao Yu, Yujia Yang, Shenghua Chai, Jinshuai Zhang, Haopeng Jin
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper presents EVID-Bench, a benchmark for detecting video misinformation through cross-video comparison, revealing significant challenges in current multimodal models' accuracy.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Video misinformation increasingly operates at the semantic and evidential level: authentic footage may be selectively edited, temporally reordered, spliced across sources, or augmented with AI-generated content to construct false narratives. Such evidence-dependent manipulations cannot be reliably verified from the input video alone, because the missing, reordered, replaced, or recontextualized evidence lies outside the video itself. We introduce \textbf{EVID-Bench}, a benchmark for search-grounded video misinformation detection, where a system must search the open web for related videos and identify what information is false through cross-video comparison. EVID-Bench comprises 222 videos spanning 9 manipulation types across 3 categories: AI generation, single-source editing, and multi-source editing. All samples are verified to be undetectable by frontier models through visual inspection alone. We evaluate nine frontier multimodal models using a retrieval-augmented verification baseline. The best system achieves only 61.43\% point-level accuracy and 43.24\% video-level accuracy, while AI-generated manipulations remain especially challenging. Error analysis reveals recurring challenges: models fixate on irrelevant anchors, misattribute synthetic content to editorial splicing, and terminate search prematurely before fully explaining the manipulation.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: AffordanceVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Empowering Action Generation through Affordance-Aware Understanding
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Qize Yu, Jiadi You, Yuran Wang, Jiaqi Liang, Bowen Ping
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: AffordanceVLA introduces a structured affordance learning framework that enhances vision-language-action models for improved robotic manipulation through precise perception-action mappings.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models leverage the rich world knowledge of pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to enable instruction-following robotic manipulation. However, the structural mismatch between VLM semantic spaces and embodied control policies often hinders the learning of precise perception-action mappings. To address this challenge, we propose AffordanceVLA, a scalable, unified framework that introduces structured affordance learning as a task-oriented and object-centric intermediate representation to establish a more precise and robust perception-action mapping. Specifically, we progressively model manipulation priors through three complementary components - Which2Act, Where2Act, and How2Act - which jointly produce spatially grounded, semantically conditioned, and action-coupled intermediate representations, thereby naturally bridging vision, language, and action. We integrate these modules into a Mixture-of-Transformer (MoT) architecture and adopt a three-stage progressive training curriculum that leverages 8.8M affordance-centric grounding and pointing samples, translating scalable vision-language supervision into improved robotic manipulation. To overcome the scarcity of dense affordance labels in robotic datasets, we also develop a robust automated data augmentation pipeline. Extensive experiments on ID & OOD simulation and real-world demonstrate that AffordanceVLA outperforms strong VLA baselines across diverse manipulation scenarios, validating structured affordance learning as a scalable and robust bridge that integrates multi-source vision-language supervision while connecting pretrained VLM semantics to embodied robot control.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: The Window Is in the Reasoning: When LLM Agents Decide to Follow Prompt Injections
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Haoxuan Jia, Yang Liu, Bin Chong, Yingguang Yang, Yancheng Chen
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The study reveals that LLM agents' responses to prompt injections are influenced by reasoning processes post-read, challenging assumptions about hijack detection and necessitating repeated task evaluations.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: LLM agents that read untrusted content can be hijacked by prompt injections. Runtime monitors that try to catch a hijack before the agent acts, and benchmarks that score each task with a single run, share an assumption: whether an agent follows an injection is settled when the injection is read. We test this assumption with branching rollouts that replay an episode exactly up to the step at which the agent reads an injection and then resample the rest of the episode many times, splitting the outcome variance into a part fixed at read time and a part decided afterwards. Across four AgentDojo suites, a Qwen3 agent without thinking is largely decided at read time (0.91 of the outcome variance lies between states); with thinking on, this share drops to 0.62 (95% CI of the drop [-0.38, -0.22]), in the same direction for three attack templates and two success labels. How much is fixed at read time is a property of the model that the same measurement reveals, and thinking lowers the attack success rate of Qwen3 but raises it for two other models. Resampling from reasoning prefixes shows that the decision forms gradually as the agent reasons. Zero-shot chain-of-thought monitors built on cheaper models miss much of what is already decided, whereas stronger monitors, and a lookahead monitor that judges simulated next actions, come close to what the prefix determines. Finally, single-run labels of thinking agents disagree with a rerun up to 35% of the time, so benchmarks need repeated runs per task.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Shape Distribution Matters: Shape-Specific Mixture-of-Experts for Amodal Segmentation Under Diverse Occlusions
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Zhixuan Li, Yujia Liu, Chen Hui, Jeonghaeng Lee, Sanghoon Lee
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: ShapeMoE introduces a shape-specific mixture-of-experts framework for amodal segmentation, enhancing performance in occluded scenes by dynamically routing objects to specialized experts based on their geometric characteristics.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Amodal segmentation aims to predict complete object masks covering both visible and occluded regions, serving as a critical foundation for robust multimedia scene understanding and interactive media editing. This task poses significant challenges in complex visual media due to severe occlusions and extreme shape variation, ranging from rigid furniture to highly deformable clothing. Existing one-size-fits-all approaches struggle to reason about diverse amodal shapes in multimedia content due to limited representation capacity. While a mixture-of-experts framework is a natural solution, naively applying it without considering the underlying shape distribution leads to mismatched routing and redundant experts. To address these issues, we introduce ShapeMoE, a shape-specific sparse mixture-of-experts framework designed for complex visual scene parsing. The key idea is to learn a latent shape distribution space and dynamically route each object to a lightweight expert tailored to its geometric characteristics. Specifically, ShapeMoE encodes each object into a compact Gaussian embedding that captures key shape features. A Shape-Aware Sparse Router then maps the object to the most suitable expert, enabling precise shape-aware routing. Each expert is lightweight and specializes in recovering occluded regions for specific shape patterns. ShapeMoE is designed for shape-specific expert specialization while maintaining computational efficiency. Extensive experiments on three challenging benchmarks demonstrate that ShapeMoE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Beyond advancing fundamental visual reasoning, ShapeMoE provides a robust and efficient visual prior for downstream multimedia applications, particularly in occlusion-heavy immersive environments.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Physical Words: A Vocabulary for Structuring Latent Reasoning in Robot Manipulation
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Jiaming Liu, Xinghao Zhu, Yiming Zhang, Shanghang Zhang, Yinxi Wang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper introduces PhysWord, a multimodal reasoning model that uses atomic action verbs to enhance robot manipulation by structuring latent reasoning and achieving high success rates in complex tasks.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Multimodal reasoning provides robotic foundation models with predictive context needed for reliable action generation. However, language-based reasoning captures task semantics but struggles to express fine-grained physical dynamics, while latent reasoning models future state evolution but offers limited structure for organizing these dynamics into reusable reasoning primitives. To bridge this gap, we introduce PhysWord, a reasoning-before-acting foundation model built on Physical Words, which use atomic action verbs as shared semantic anchors for continuous representations of physical dynamics. Specifically, PhysWord predicts upcoming atomic action words and directly aligns their contextual hidden states with latent targets derived from the corresponding future observations. Building on these primitives, we construct a temporally structured PhysWord space with visual and optional tactile variants of each action word. Autoregressively predicting Physical Words across future timesteps captures transitions between execution stages, providing structured multimodal context for action generation. PhysWord achieves state-of-the-art success rates of 90.3\% on visuotactile UniVTAC and 99.6\% on vision-based LIBERO-Long, and outperforms competing methods on real-world tasks using bimanual grippers and dexterous hands. Further evaluations demonstrate that our structured latent reasoning framework generalizes to unseen scenarios and enables long-horizon manipulation.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: HandsOn: A Large-Scale Simulation Benchmark for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Tianwei Luo, Yiming He, Hongjin Wu, Ting Pan, Debin Ren
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: HandsOn is a comprehensive simulation benchmark for dexterous manipulation, featuring diverse robotic platforms and tasks to evaluate generalization and sim-to-real transfer in manipulation skills.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: General-purpose manipulation requires reliable behavior across embodiments, objects, and task demands. We introduce HandsOn, a composable simulation platform and benchmark for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation. It supports five robotic arms, six dexterous hands, and approximately 200 rigid, articulated, and deformable assets in randomized scenes. The benchmark pairs 18,000 curated human demonstrations with 66 human-verified tasks: Core-50 supports demonstration-based learning and execution tests, while Transfer-16 evaluates asset and relation transfer, skill composition, and deformable manipulation without target-task training demonstrations. Qualitative real-robot rollouts illustrate sim-to-real transfer. Across diffusion, vision-language-action, world-action, and prompted VLM-based methods, the best trained multi-task policy achieves 29.1% Core-50 success. Without benchmark finetuning, GPT-6 using move_eef for palm-and-finger control achieves 5.2% on Core-50 and 1.9% on Transfer-16 over 660 trials. Trained-policy stage diagnostics expose failures in contact establishment, action coordination, and maintaining achieved goals, with additional sequencing errors in composed tasks. HandsOn provides a shared basis for investigating manipulation generalization and the limits of reliable physical interaction.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Zhaoxi Zhang, Hao Liang, Linxuan Wu, Yiming Wu, Yifu Yuan
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: SpatialScout is a benchmark assessing vision-language model agents' ability to actively explore and accurately map 3D scenes, revealing significant limitations in current models' performance.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world. Yet spatial question answering offers limited evidence of whether models can construct accurate metric maps through autonomous exploration. We introduce SpatialScout, a benchmark for evaluating vision-language model (VLM) agents on active object-level 3D mapping. SpatialScout comprises 80 diverse indoor scenes containing 3,140 target objects. Given an object inventory, RGB observations, camera calibration, and camera poses, agents control a camera to explore each scene and estimate object centers in a shared coordinate frame. The task requires coordinating viewpoint selection, cross-view association, geometric estimation, and map revision under bounded interaction budgets. Evaluation jointly measures localization accuracy and target coverage through object-scale overlap scores that penalize missing predictions. Experiments with frontier VLMs reveal substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated model, Claude Opus 5.5, achieves a mean overlap score of 41.71%, with 47.23% of targets exceeding an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 and only 3.25% exceeding 0.9. These results reveal a substantial gap between recovering coarse object layouts and constructing complete, precise metric maps. SpatialScout provides a quantitative testbed for developing agents that build reliable 3D spatial representations through active perception. Code is available at https://github.com/JesseZZZZZ/SpatialScout.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Xinhao Ji, Hui En Pang, Hao Li, Kairui Hu, Jiner Wang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: EgoXperience introduces a comprehensive framework for learning coherent egocentric representations from video, achieving significant improvements in joint reconstruction and object pose estimation.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Reconstructing human activity from egocentric video requires more than recovering individual 3D components: the observer's motion, surrounding geometry, and hand-object interactions must fit together in a consistent world. Achieving this coherence requires both joint reconstruction and aligned supervision, yet existing methods and datasets offer limited support for either. We present EgoXperience, a full-stack paradigm that addresses these needs through data collection, automatic annotation, unified modeling, and benchmarking. Central to EgoXperience is an automatic annotation engine, EgoX-Engine, that couples geometrically verified object tracking with SLAM-based world alignment, yielding consistent supervision for the camera, scene, hands, and objects. This yields EgoX-Data-6M, a 50-hour dataset of task-driven manipulation and locomotion within and across indoor and outdoor environments, with second-level task captions. We carefully select one hour across these activity categories as EgoX-Bench to evaluate joint reconstruction. To translate this supervision into reconstruction, we introduce EgoX, trained with EgoX-Data-6M and complementary annotations from additional public datasets. Given monocular egocentric video and first-frame object masks, our model achieves joint metric reconstruction of the camera, scene, hands, and objects in a shared world coordinate frame with a single forward pass. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across scene estimation and world-space hand-object pose recovery. Against the strongest evaluated baselines, EgoX reduces camera, hand, and depth errors by 68.9%, 65.6%, and 42.9%, and improves object pose scores by 28.0%.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: LayerRoute: Action-Conditioned Mixture-of-Layers Routing for Vision-Language-Action Policies
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Zheng Lu, Haoran Liao, Wanqi Zhong, Yunhe Ni, Lijie Wang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: LayerRoute enhances Vision-Language-Action policies by enabling adaptive routing of visual-semantic representations and action states, improving performance with minimal parameter increase.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies leverage pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to guide action generation for robot control. VLMs provide hierarchical visual-semantic representations that evolve across layers, from local visual geometry to abstract, language-aligned semantics; different manipulation tasks may therefore require different mixtures of layer representations. Meanwhile, the action module maintains intermediate representations that evolve throughout action computation and may provide useful information for subsequent decisions. However, existing VLA interfaces offer limited flexibility in representation access: VLM information is exposed through fixed layer assignments for each action layer, while intermediate action states are only propagated implicitly through residual streams without explicit reuse. We introduce LayerRoute, an action-conditioned representation routing interface that enables adaptive access to VLM layers and action representations. The Layer Mixture Router dynamically forms mixtures of cached VLM representations, while Action-State Reread reuses earlier action representations. Across diverse simulation and real-world benchmarks, LayerRoute consistently improves StarVLA-$π$ and $π_{0.5}$, achieving up to 7.2 gains on LIBERO Long with only 0.31% / 3.87% additional parameters. Ablation studies validate the benefit of action-conditioned layer routing, while routing analyses reveal structured allocation patterns across action layers and task settings.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Planning Takes More Than Token Prediction: Causal Plan for Benchmarking and Building Physically Grounded Embodied Reasoners
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Zheng Lu, Mingqi Gao, Qinlei Xie, Wanqi Zhong, Hanwen Cui
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper introduces Causal-Plan-Bench and Causal Planner, emphasizing the need for physically grounded causal reasoning over token prediction in embodied vision-language planning.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Current benchmarks for embodied vision-language planning inadvertently favor linguistic next-token prediction over physically grounded next-state reasoning. This rewards models that mimic statistical language priors rather than track true causal dependencies, reducing complex physical planning to shallow sequence modeling. Hence, achieving genuine physical autonomy requires a fundamental shift from linguistically grounded token prediction toward physically grounded causal reasoning. To this end, we introduce Causal-Plan-Bench, a high-fidelity diagnostic suite spanning four causal dimensions, curated via multi-stage verification. To endow models with this capability, a four-stage annotation pipeline extracts structured interaction records from egocentric videos to construct Causal-Plan-1M, a dense million-scale corpus of explicit causal reasoning traces. Extensive evaluation reveals a striking gap: leading models struggle to demonstrate genuine physical agency -- even GPT-6-astra scores only 43.04. In contrast, our tailored training recipe enables Causal Planner to internalize the complex physical logic required for accurate next-state estimation. Built upon Qwen3-VL-8B, Causal Planner raises its backbone's score from 33.23 to 45.28, a 36.3% relative gain, and improves on three external benchmarks without benchmark-specific adaptation. We further observe an empirical Causal-Supervision Scaling Trend. Paired no-vision controls also reveal substantial visual dependence, while cross-judge comparisons and human scoring assess the reliability of automated evaluation. More importantly, we initiate the first effort to turn agents from superficial token predictors into physically grounded causal reasoners, bridging language modeling and world modeling.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: AVTime: Reinforcing Dense Audio-Visual Captions with Bidirectional Alignment
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Mingyang Wu, Kaituo Feng, Bohao Li, Kaixiong Gong, Zihao Yin
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper introduces AVTime, a model and dataset for dense audio-visual captioning that enhances temporal and semantic alignment through a novel evaluation benchmark.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Dense temporal audio-visual captioning is important for multimodal video understanding and generation. However, prior work is constrained by three main limitations: (1) the lack of a dataset combining high temporal resolution, longer videos, and bidirectional alignment between time and events; (2) the reliance of most existing RL methods on checklists; and (3) the lack of a benchmark that bidirectionally evaluates event semantic correctness and temporal accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose: (1) AVTime-50K, a high-quality 50K-scale dataset with temporally precise, semantically accurate captions and longer videos; (2) AVTime, a state-of-the-art model optimized with a novel Bidirectional Temporal-Semantic Alignment (BiTSA) reward that imposes explicit bidirectional constraints between time and events; and (3) AVTime-Bench, a specialized benchmark that introduces a novel bidirectional evaluation of temporal accuracy and semantic correctness. Our code, models, and datasets are available at https://huggingface.co/collections/Apryle/avtime.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: TESS: LLM-guided Translation, Exploration, Simulation, and Search for Embodied Task Planning
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Peiran Xu, Yixiang Yang, Jinghan Li, Fei Li, Cao Sheng
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper presents TESS, an LLM-guided search algorithm that enhances embodied task planning by integrating commonsense knowledge for efficient exploration and action selection in complex environments.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: In this work we focus on the problem of embodied task planning, which requires an agent to accomplish a complex task by separating it into atomic actions. Recent studies have developed LLM-based methods to address this problem. However, the executability and correctness of the generated plans remain suboptimal in complex environments and tasks. On the other hand, classical search algorithms have the potential to solve the planning problems perfectly, yet they require fully observable environments, known state transitions and goal state, which are often unattainable in general task domains. Therefore, we propose to implement an LLM-guided search algorithm that makes the search process possible and efficient by incorporating LLMs' commonsense knowledge. Our method leverages LLMs to (1) translate natural language instructions into formatted goal conditions, (2) facilitate efficient exploration in partially observable environments, (3) implement a rule-based world simulator, and (4) prune the space of candidate actions to improve search efficiency. Experimental results on VirtualHome and ALFWorld demonstrate its superior performance.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: CoEvolve: Self-Evolving Code Policies from Skills to Strategies for Humanoid Robots
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Zicheng Liu, Haochen Wu, Jiawei He, Suyun Zhao, Huan Yang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: CoEvolve is a framework enabling humanoid robots to adaptively coordinate through executable code, enhancing multi-robot collaboration in complex tasks despite physical execution deviations.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Recent advances in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and World Action Models (WAMs) have expanded the manipulation and whole body capabilities of individual robots. Yet a single robot remains limited by its embodiment, and many real world tasks require capabilities that can only emerge through cooperation. Existing multi robot frameworks largely emphasize task decomposition, allocation, and replanning, while providing limited support for adapting executable coordination when physical execution deviates from the intended behavior. We present CoEvolve, a framework that represents team coordination as executable code over fixed robot motor skills. CoEvolve introduces Verifier Guided Coordination Evolution, where a multimodal foundation model instantiates coordination strategies through motion primitives, semantic objectives, temporary robot roles, and bounded execution parameters. Physical verification evaluates each executed transition, rejected behaviors trigger structured coordination revision from an accepted checkpoint, and verified experience is retained to guide subsequent decisions. We evaluate CoEvolve with two simulated Unitree G1 humanoids transporting a freely supported rigid payload through constrained corridors. Across 15 base task runs with three multimodal backbone families, CoEvolve completes 8 tasks, with every backbone achieving end to end success. Additional evaluations yield verified placement on two additional corridor layouts and after both same-backbone and cross-backbone experience initialization, while exposing persistent limitations in motion precision and contact stability. These results support executable coordination as a practical interface for adapting long horizon multi robot collaboration under shared physical constraints.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Jiadi You, Qize Yu, Yue Chen, Minghong Cai, Zhide Zhong
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: AffordanceWAM is a generative model that enhances robot manipulation by integrating affordance-aware predictions from diverse human videos and robot actions for improved interaction and performance.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Generalizable robot manipulation requires predicting how a scene will evolve, identifying where interactions are feasible, and determining how to act. Action-labeled robot videos directly supervise control but are costly and limited in diversity, whereas egocentric human videos capture diverse interactions but lack robot actions and differ in embodiment and appearance. We introduce AffordanceWAM, an affordance-aware generative World Action Model that represents object-centric spatiotemporal affordance through Scalar Affordance and Affordance Heatmap, within the generated future World. This representation grounds visual prediction in task-relevantant objects and interaction regions for action generation, and provides shared interaction targets across human and robot videos. Built on a pretrained video diffusion Transformer, AffordanceWAM uses separately parameterized World and Action Experts, coupled through Masked Joint Self-Attention, to jointly predict future RGB observations, Scalar Affordance fields, Affordance Heatmaps, and continuous robot actions under a unified flow-matching objective. Human videos supervise all three future-World streams, whereas robot trajectories additionally provide action supervision, enabling transfer without human action labels or retargeting. Experiments on RoboCasa, CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D, and real-world manipulation demonstrate consistent gains over RGB-only and robot-data-only baselines. Under fixed robot supervision, RoboCasa performance improves monotonically as affordance-annotated human video scales. These results support affordance as an effective interface for both vision-language-action learning and human-to-robot transfer.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Beyond Explicit Intent: Discovering and Shaping Artistic Intent through Human-AI Co-Creation
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Renye Yan, Jialun Zhong, Jikang Cheng, Yi Gao, Yanzeng Li
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper presents a human-AI co-creation framework that enhances artistic intent discovery and shaping by allowing artists to explore and refine preferences through interaction with generative AI.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Generative AI is becoming an important medium for artistic creation, yet existing interactions often assume that creators can specify intentions in advance and accurately communicate them through text prompts. Artistic intentions, however, may be vague, latent, or recognizable only after seeing concrete visual possibilities. We propose a human-AI co-creation paradigm beyond explicit intent expression. By expanding model exploration, we expose artists to diverse visual possibilities, allowing them to identify previously unarticulated preferences through observation, comparison, and selection. We then integrate artists' curatorial judgments into reinforcement learning, assigning different learning strengths based on preferences over generation trajectories, so recognized directions are more strongly reinforced and the model gradually adapts to individual aesthetics. This creates a continuous "explore-identify-shape-re-explore" loop in which artistic intent is progressively discovered, externalized, and shaped. Through three user studies, we examine latent-preference discovery, personalized preference alignment, and the externalization of vague, difficult-to-express creative intentions.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: RL Teaches VLMs Where to Attend but Not How to Perceive
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Ziqian Zhang, Junjie Liao, Zhining Zhang, Wentao Zhu
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: Reinforcement learning enhances Vision-Language Models' task success by improving attention to visual information, but does not significantly boost their grounded visual understanding capabilities.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Although reinforcement learning (RL) effectively trains Vision-Language Model (VLM) agents, the mechanisms behind these capability gains are poorly understood. Across four diverse agent environments, we investigate whether the task-success gains from multi-turn RL are accompanied by improved grounded visual question answering about the environment. To assess this, we design environment-specific grounded VQA tasks that reveal improvements in grounded visual understanding. Representational probing shows that vision-encoder probe accuracy remains relatively stable, while LLM-layer probe accuracy improves. Attention analysis further reveals that LLM layers pay more attention to visual tokens during RL training. To test whether increased attention to visual tokens contributes to VQA gains, we introduce a lightweight plug-and-play intervention using a fixed attention bias. Without updating model parameters or computing gradients, this intervention partially restores VQA gains on the untrained model. These results reveal better utilization of visual information as a key mechanism behind the gains from RL.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: HAF-VLA: Hierarchical Action Flow Framework for Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Control
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Langzhe Gu, Chengkai Hou, Meng Li, Xinhua Wang, Xinyuan Lv
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: HAF-VLA is a hierarchical framework that enhances humanoid robots' vision-language-action control by progressively refining locomotion and manipulation actions through cross-stage conditioning.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Humanoid robots hold great promise as general-purpose agents in human-centered environments, yet adapting generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policies to real-world humanoid loco-manipulation remains challenging. Unlike fixed-base or wheeled manipulators, humanoids must coordinate locomotion, posture, gaze, and dual-arm manipulation over a high-dimensional whole-body action space, where inaccurate base or waist motions can easily induce unstable and aggressive upper-body compensation. We propose HAF-VLA, a hierarchical action-flow framework for humanoid VLA control. Built upon a pretrained flow-matching VLA, HAF-VLA inherits the vision-language prefix encoder and action expert weights, and adapts them to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation with learnable stage embeddings and cross-stage KV-cache conditioning. Instead of generating the full action chunk in a single pass, HAF-VLA progressively denoises a shared whole-body action space: first locomotion and head commands, then waist refinement, and finally full-body manipulation. To preserve structural dependencies across stages, we introduce a cross-stage KV cache conditioning mechanism, enabling subsequent action generation stages to refine and augment their outputs based on the action representations from preceding stages. Experimental results across six real-world tasks demonstrate that our framework significantly enhances the performance of existing models in humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, demonstrating an effective pathway for adapting strong mobile-manipulation VLAs to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: RIFAR: Reliability-Informed and Forgetting-Aware Replay for Continual Robot Learning with World-Action Models
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Tu Lin, Zheng Lu, Zirui Song, Zixian Lin, Zebang Feng
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: RIFAR enhances continual robot learning by using reliability-informed generative replay to efficiently adapt to new tasks while minimizing catastrophic forgetting and action drift.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Genuine embodied agency requires robots to turn continuous real-world experience into lasting, transferable skills. This demands continual learning that integrates new capabilities while preserving prior knowledge in evolving environments. Experience replay mitigates catastrophic forgetting, but storing complete demonstrations becomes costly as tasks accumulate. World-action models provide an alternative through generative replay. However, visually coherent rollouts may contain actions that cannot realize the predicted transitions, while new-task adaptation can disrupt learned behavior. To address these problems, we propose RIFAR (Reliability-Informed and Forgetting-Aware Replay), a reliability-informed and drift-aware generative replay framework. It reconstructs trajectories from compact historical demonstration prefixes and uses a trainable inverse-dynamics model to assess action-visual consistency. It first adapts to new tasks using current-task demonstrations and high-reliability replay, then evaluates how this adaptation changes action predictions on historical inputs and prioritizes reliable trajectories with greater action drift for further training. Across three LIBERO suites and real-world experiments, RIFAR outperforms the previous state of the art in WAM-based generative replay. On LIBERO-Goal, it achieves an AUC of 90.97 while retaining only 320 historical time steps per task, about 4.9% of those retained by 50-demonstration replay.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: When Seeing Is Not Believing -- A Benchmark for Search-Grounded Video Misinformation Detection
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Tao Yu, Yujia Yang, Shenghua Chai, Jinshuai Zhang, Haopeng Jin
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper presents EVID-Bench, a benchmark for detecting video misinformation through cross-video comparison, revealing significant challenges in current multimodal models' accuracy.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Video misinformation increasingly operates at the semantic and evidential level: authentic footage may be selectively edited, temporally reordered, spliced across sources, or augmented with AI-generated content to construct false narratives. Such evidence-dependent manipulations cannot be reliably verified from the input video alone, because the missing, reordered, replaced, or recontextualized evidence lies outside the video itself. We introduce \textbf{EVID-Bench}, a benchmark for search-grounded video misinformation detection, where a system must search the open web for related videos and identify what information is false through cross-video comparison. EVID-Bench comprises 222 videos spanning 9 manipulation types across 3 categories: AI generation, single-source editing, and multi-source editing. All samples are verified to be undetectable by frontier models through visual inspection alone. We evaluate nine frontier multimodal models using a retrieval-augmented verification baseline. The best system achieves only 61.43\% point-level accuracy and 43.24\% video-level accuracy, while AI-generated manipulations remain especially challenging. Error analysis reveals recurring challenges: models fixate on irrelevant anchors, misattribute synthetic content to editorial splicing, and terminate search prematurely before fully explaining the manipulation.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: AffordanceVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Empowering Action Generation through Affordance-Aware Understanding
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Qize Yu, Jiadi You, Yuran Wang, Jiaqi Liang, Bowen Ping
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: AffordanceVLA introduces a structured affordance learning framework that enhances vision-language-action models for improved robotic manipulation through precise perception-action mappings.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models leverage the rich world knowledge of pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to enable instruction-following robotic manipulation. However, the structural mismatch between VLM semantic spaces and embodied control policies often hinders the learning of precise perception-action mappings. To address this challenge, we propose AffordanceVLA, a scalable, unified framework that introduces structured affordance learning as a task-oriented and object-centric intermediate representation to establish a more precise and robust perception-action mapping. Specifically, we progressively model manipulation priors through three complementary components - Which2Act, Where2Act, and How2Act - which jointly produce spatially grounded, semantically conditioned, and action-coupled intermediate representations, thereby naturally bridging vision, language, and action. We integrate these modules into a Mixture-of-Transformer (MoT) architecture and adopt a three-stage progressive training curriculum that leverages 8.8M affordance-centric grounding and pointing samples, translating scalable vision-language supervision into improved robotic manipulation. To overcome the scarcity of dense affordance labels in robotic datasets, we also develop a robust automated data augmentation pipeline. Extensive experiments on ID & OOD simulation and real-world demonstrate that AffordanceVLA outperforms strong VLA baselines across diverse manipulation scenarios, validating structured affordance learning as a scalable and robust bridge that integrates multi-source vision-language supervision while connecting pretrained VLM semantics to embodied robot control.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: The Window Is in the Reasoning: When LLM Agents Decide to Follow Prompt Injections
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Haoxuan Jia, Yang Liu, Bin Chong, Yingguang Yang, Yancheng Chen
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The study reveals that LLM agents' responses to prompt injections are influenced by reasoning processes post-read, challenging assumptions about hijack detection and necessitating repeated task evaluations.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: LLM agents that read untrusted content can be hijacked by prompt injections. Runtime monitors that try to catch a hijack before the agent acts, and benchmarks that score each task with a single run, share an assumption: whether an agent follows an injection is settled when the injection is read. We test this assumption with branching rollouts that replay an episode exactly up to the step at which the agent reads an injection and then resample the rest of the episode many times, splitting the outcome variance into a part fixed at read time and a part decided afterwards. Across four AgentDojo suites, a Qwen3 agent without thinking is largely decided at read time (0.91 of the outcome variance lies between states); with thinking on, this share drops to 0.62 (95% CI of the drop [-0.38, -0.22]), in the same direction for three attack templates and two success labels. How much is fixed at read time is a property of the model that the same measurement reveals, and thinking lowers the attack success rate of Qwen3 but raises it for two other models. Resampling from reasoning prefixes shows that the decision forms gradually as the agent reasons. Zero-shot chain-of-thought monitors built on cheaper models miss much of what is already decided, whereas stronger monitors, and a lookahead monitor that judges simulated next actions, come close to what the prefix determines. Finally, single-run labels of thinking agents disagree with a rerun up to 35% of the time, so benchmarks need repeated runs per task.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Shape Distribution Matters: Shape-Specific Mixture-of-Experts for Amodal Segmentation Under Diverse Occlusions
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Zhixuan Li, Yujia Liu, Chen Hui, Jeonghaeng Lee, Sanghoon Lee
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: ShapeMoE introduces a shape-specific mixture-of-experts framework for amodal segmentation, enhancing performance in occluded scenes by dynamically routing objects to specialized experts based on their geometric characteristics.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Amodal segmentation aims to predict complete object masks covering both visible and occluded regions, serving as a critical foundation for robust multimedia scene understanding and interactive media editing. This task poses significant challenges in complex visual media due to severe occlusions and extreme shape variation, ranging from rigid furniture to highly deformable clothing. Existing one-size-fits-all approaches struggle to reason about diverse amodal shapes in multimedia content due to limited representation capacity. While a mixture-of-experts framework is a natural solution, naively applying it without considering the underlying shape distribution leads to mismatched routing and redundant experts. To address these issues, we introduce ShapeMoE, a shape-specific sparse mixture-of-experts framework designed for complex visual scene parsing. The key idea is to learn a latent shape distribution space and dynamically route each object to a lightweight expert tailored to its geometric characteristics. Specifically, ShapeMoE encodes each object into a compact Gaussian embedding that captures key shape features. A Shape-Aware Sparse Router then maps the object to the most suitable expert, enabling precise shape-aware routing. Each expert is lightweight and specializes in recovering occluded regions for specific shape patterns. ShapeMoE is designed for shape-specific expert specialization while maintaining computational efficiency. Extensive experiments on three challenging benchmarks demonstrate that ShapeMoE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Beyond advancing fundamental visual reasoning, ShapeMoE provides a robust and efficient visual prior for downstream multimedia applications, particularly in occlusion-heavy immersive environments.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Physical Words: A Vocabulary for Structuring Latent Reasoning in Robot Manipulation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Jiaming Liu, Xinghao Zhu, Yiming Zhang, Shanghang Zhang, Yinxi Wang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper introduces PhysWord, a multimodal reasoning model that uses atomic action verbs to enhance robot manipulation by structuring latent reasoning and achieving high success rates in complex tasks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Multimodal reasoning provides robotic foundation models with predictive context needed for reliable action generation. However, language-based reasoning captures task semantics but struggles to express fine-grained physical dynamics, while latent reasoning models future state evolution but offers limited structure for organizing these dynamics into reusable reasoning primitives. To bridge this gap, we introduce PhysWord, a reasoning-before-acting foundation model built on Physical Words, which use atomic action verbs as shared semantic anchors for continuous representations of physical dynamics. Specifically, PhysWord predicts upcoming atomic action words and directly aligns their contextual hidden states with latent targets derived from the corresponding future observations. Building on these primitives, we construct a temporally structured PhysWord space with visual and optional tactile variants of each action word. Autoregressively predicting Physical Words across future timesteps captures transitions between execution stages, providing structured multimodal context for action generation. PhysWord achieves state-of-the-art success rates of 90.3\% on visuotactile UniVTAC and 99.6\% on vision-based LIBERO-Long, and outperforms competing methods on real-world tasks using bimanual grippers and dexterous hands. Further evaluations demonstrate that our structured latent reasoning framework generalizes to unseen scenarios and enables long-horizon manipulation.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: HandsOn: A Large-Scale Simulation Benchmark for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Tianwei Luo, Yiming He, Hongjin Wu, Ting Pan, Debin Ren
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: HandsOn is a comprehensive simulation benchmark for dexterous manipulation, featuring diverse robotic platforms and tasks to evaluate generalization and sim-to-real transfer in manipulation skills.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: General-purpose manipulation requires reliable behavior across embodiments, objects, and task demands. We introduce HandsOn, a composable simulation platform and benchmark for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation. It supports five robotic arms, six dexterous hands, and approximately 200 rigid, articulated, and deformable assets in randomized scenes. The benchmark pairs 18,000 curated human demonstrations with 66 human-verified tasks: Core-50 supports demonstration-based learning and execution tests, while Transfer-16 evaluates asset and relation transfer, skill composition, and deformable manipulation without target-task training demonstrations. Qualitative real-robot rollouts illustrate sim-to-real transfer. Across diffusion, vision-language-action, world-action, and prompted VLM-based methods, the best trained multi-task policy achieves 29.1% Core-50 success. Without benchmark finetuning, GPT-6 using move_eef for palm-and-finger control achieves 5.2% on Core-50 and 1.9% on Transfer-16 over 660 trials. Trained-policy stage diagnostics expose failures in contact establishment, action coordination, and maintaining achieved goals, with additional sequencing errors in composed tasks. HandsOn provides a shared basis for investigating manipulation generalization and the limits of reliable physical interaction.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Zhaoxi Zhang, Hao Liang, Linxuan Wu, Yiming Wu, Yifu Yuan
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: SpatialScout is a benchmark assessing vision-language model agents' ability to actively explore and accurately map 3D scenes, revealing significant limitations in current models' performance.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world. Yet spatial question answering offers limited evidence of whether models can construct accurate metric maps through autonomous exploration. We introduce SpatialScout, a benchmark for evaluating vision-language model (VLM) agents on active object-level 3D mapping. SpatialScout comprises 80 diverse indoor scenes containing 3,140 target objects. Given an object inventory, RGB observations, camera calibration, and camera poses, agents control a camera to explore each scene and estimate object centers in a shared coordinate frame. The task requires coordinating viewpoint selection, cross-view association, geometric estimation, and map revision under bounded interaction budgets. Evaluation jointly measures localization accuracy and target coverage through object-scale overlap scores that penalize missing predictions. Experiments with frontier VLMs reveal substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated model, Claude Opus 5.5, achieves a mean overlap score of 41.71%, with 47.23% of targets exceeding an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 and only 3.25% exceeding 0.9. These results reveal a substantial gap between recovering coarse object layouts and constructing complete, precise metric maps. SpatialScout provides a quantitative testbed for developing agents that build reliable 3D spatial representations through active perception. Code is available at https://github.com/JesseZZZZZ/SpatialScout.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Xinhao Ji, Hui En Pang, Hao Li, Kairui Hu, Jiner Wang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: EgoXperience introduces a comprehensive framework for learning coherent egocentric representations from video, achieving significant improvements in joint reconstruction and object pose estimation.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Reconstructing human activity from egocentric video requires more than recovering individual 3D components: the observer's motion, surrounding geometry, and hand-object interactions must fit together in a consistent world. Achieving this coherence requires both joint reconstruction and aligned supervision, yet existing methods and datasets offer limited support for either. We present EgoXperience, a full-stack paradigm that addresses these needs through data collection, automatic annotation, unified modeling, and benchmarking. Central to EgoXperience is an automatic annotation engine, EgoX-Engine, that couples geometrically verified object tracking with SLAM-based world alignment, yielding consistent supervision for the camera, scene, hands, and objects. This yields EgoX-Data-6M, a 50-hour dataset of task-driven manipulation and locomotion within and across indoor and outdoor environments, with second-level task captions. We carefully select one hour across these activity categories as EgoX-Bench to evaluate joint reconstruction. To translate this supervision into reconstruction, we introduce EgoX, trained with EgoX-Data-6M and complementary annotations from additional public datasets. Given monocular egocentric video and first-frame object masks, our model achieves joint metric reconstruction of the camera, scene, hands, and objects in a shared world coordinate frame with a single forward pass. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across scene estimation and world-space hand-object pose recovery. Against the strongest evaluated baselines, EgoX reduces camera, hand, and depth errors by 68.9%, 65.6%, and 42.9%, and improves object pose scores by 28.0%.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: LayerRoute: Action-Conditioned Mixture-of-Layers Routing for Vision-Language-Action Policies
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Zheng Lu, Haoran Liao, Wanqi Zhong, Yunhe Ni, Lijie Wang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: LayerRoute enhances Vision-Language-Action policies by enabling adaptive routing of visual-semantic representations and action states, improving performance with minimal parameter increase.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies leverage pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to guide action generation for robot control. VLMs provide hierarchical visual-semantic representations that evolve across layers, from local visual geometry to abstract, language-aligned semantics; different manipulation tasks may therefore require different mixtures of layer representations. Meanwhile, the action module maintains intermediate representations that evolve throughout action computation and may provide useful information for subsequent decisions. However, existing VLA interfaces offer limited flexibility in representation access: VLM information is exposed through fixed layer assignments for each action layer, while intermediate action states are only propagated implicitly through residual streams without explicit reuse. We introduce LayerRoute, an action-conditioned representation routing interface that enables adaptive access to VLM layers and action representations. The Layer Mixture Router dynamically forms mixtures of cached VLM representations, while Action-State Reread reuses earlier action representations. Across diverse simulation and real-world benchmarks, LayerRoute consistently improves StarVLA-$π$ and $π_{0.5}$, achieving up to 7.2 gains on LIBERO Long with only 0.31% / 3.87% additional parameters. Ablation studies validate the benefit of action-conditioned layer routing, while routing analyses reveal structured allocation patterns across action layers and task settings.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Planning Takes More Than Token Prediction: Causal Plan for Benchmarking and Building Physically Grounded Embodied Reasoners
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Zheng Lu, Mingqi Gao, Qinlei Xie, Wanqi Zhong, Hanwen Cui
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper introduces Causal-Plan-Bench and Causal Planner, emphasizing the need for physically grounded causal reasoning over token prediction in embodied vision-language planning.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Current benchmarks for embodied vision-language planning inadvertently favor linguistic next-token prediction over physically grounded next-state reasoning. This rewards models that mimic statistical language priors rather than track true causal dependencies, reducing complex physical planning to shallow sequence modeling. Hence, achieving genuine physical autonomy requires a fundamental shift from linguistically grounded token prediction toward physically grounded causal reasoning. To this end, we introduce Causal-Plan-Bench, a high-fidelity diagnostic suite spanning four causal dimensions, curated via multi-stage verification. To endow models with this capability, a four-stage annotation pipeline extracts structured interaction records from egocentric videos to construct Causal-Plan-1M, a dense million-scale corpus of explicit causal reasoning traces. Extensive evaluation reveals a striking gap: leading models struggle to demonstrate genuine physical agency -- even GPT-6-astra scores only 43.04. In contrast, our tailored training recipe enables Causal Planner to internalize the complex physical logic required for accurate next-state estimation. Built upon Qwen3-VL-8B, Causal Planner raises its backbone's score from 33.23 to 45.28, a 36.3% relative gain, and improves on three external benchmarks without benchmark-specific adaptation. We further observe an empirical Causal-Supervision Scaling Trend. Paired no-vision controls also reveal substantial visual dependence, while cross-judge comparisons and human scoring assess the reliability of automated evaluation. More importantly, we initiate the first effort to turn agents from superficial token predictors into physically grounded causal reasoners, bridging language modeling and world modeling.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: AVTime: Reinforcing Dense Audio-Visual Captions with Bidirectional Alignment
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Mingyang Wu, Kaituo Feng, Bohao Li, Kaixiong Gong, Zihao Yin
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper introduces AVTime, a model and dataset for dense audio-visual captioning that enhances temporal and semantic alignment through a novel evaluation benchmark.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Dense temporal audio-visual captioning is important for multimodal video understanding and generation. However, prior work is constrained by three main limitations: (1) the lack of a dataset combining high temporal resolution, longer videos, and bidirectional alignment between time and events; (2) the reliance of most existing RL methods on checklists; and (3) the lack of a benchmark that bidirectionally evaluates event semantic correctness and temporal accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose: (1) AVTime-50K, a high-quality 50K-scale dataset with temporally precise, semantically accurate captions and longer videos; (2) AVTime, a state-of-the-art model optimized with a novel Bidirectional Temporal-Semantic Alignment (BiTSA) reward that imposes explicit bidirectional constraints between time and events; and (3) AVTime-Bench, a specialized benchmark that introduces a novel bidirectional evaluation of temporal accuracy and semantic correctness. Our code, models, and datasets are available at https://huggingface.co/collections/Apryle/avtime.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: TESS: LLM-guided Translation, Exploration, Simulation, and Search for Embodied Task Planning
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Peiran Xu, Yixiang Yang, Jinghan Li, Fei Li, Cao Sheng
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper presents TESS, an LLM-guided search algorithm that enhances embodied task planning by integrating commonsense knowledge for efficient exploration and action selection in complex environments.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: In this work we focus on the problem of embodied task planning, which requires an agent to accomplish a complex task by separating it into atomic actions. Recent studies have developed LLM-based methods to address this problem. However, the executability and correctness of the generated plans remain suboptimal in complex environments and tasks. On the other hand, classical search algorithms have the potential to solve the planning problems perfectly, yet they require fully observable environments, known state transitions and goal state, which are often unattainable in general task domains. Therefore, we propose to implement an LLM-guided search algorithm that makes the search process possible and efficient by incorporating LLMs' commonsense knowledge. Our method leverages LLMs to (1) translate natural language instructions into formatted goal conditions, (2) facilitate efficient exploration in partially observable environments, (3) implement a rule-based world simulator, and (4) prune the space of candidate actions to improve search efficiency. Experimental results on VirtualHome and ALFWorld demonstrate its superior performance.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: CoEvolve: Self-Evolving Code Policies from Skills to Strategies for Humanoid Robots
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Zicheng Liu, Haochen Wu, Jiawei He, Suyun Zhao, Huan Yang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: CoEvolve is a framework enabling humanoid robots to adaptively coordinate through executable code, enhancing multi-robot collaboration in complex tasks despite physical execution deviations.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Recent advances in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and World Action Models (WAMs) have expanded the manipulation and whole body capabilities of individual robots. Yet a single robot remains limited by its embodiment, and many real world tasks require capabilities that can only emerge through cooperation. Existing multi robot frameworks largely emphasize task decomposition, allocation, and replanning, while providing limited support for adapting executable coordination when physical execution deviates from the intended behavior. We present CoEvolve, a framework that represents team coordination as executable code over fixed robot motor skills. CoEvolve introduces Verifier Guided Coordination Evolution, where a multimodal foundation model instantiates coordination strategies through motion primitives, semantic objectives, temporary robot roles, and bounded execution parameters. Physical verification evaluates each executed transition, rejected behaviors trigger structured coordination revision from an accepted checkpoint, and verified experience is retained to guide subsequent decisions. We evaluate CoEvolve with two simulated Unitree G1 humanoids transporting a freely supported rigid payload through constrained corridors. Across 15 base task runs with three multimodal backbone families, CoEvolve completes 8 tasks, with every backbone achieving end to end success. Additional evaluations yield verified placement on two additional corridor layouts and after both same-backbone and cross-backbone experience initialization, while exposing persistent limitations in motion precision and contact stability. These results support executable coordination as a practical interface for adapting long horizon multi robot collaboration under shared physical constraints.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Jiadi You, Qize Yu, Yue Chen, Minghong Cai, Zhide Zhong
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: AffordanceWAM is a generative model that enhances robot manipulation by integrating affordance-aware predictions from diverse human videos and robot actions for improved interaction and performance.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Generalizable robot manipulation requires predicting how a scene will evolve, identifying where interactions are feasible, and determining how to act. Action-labeled robot videos directly supervise control but are costly and limited in diversity, whereas egocentric human videos capture diverse interactions but lack robot actions and differ in embodiment and appearance. We introduce AffordanceWAM, an affordance-aware generative World Action Model that represents object-centric spatiotemporal affordance through Scalar Affordance and Affordance Heatmap, within the generated future World. This representation grounds visual prediction in task-relevantant objects and interaction regions for action generation, and provides shared interaction targets across human and robot videos. Built on a pretrained video diffusion Transformer, AffordanceWAM uses separately parameterized World and Action Experts, coupled through Masked Joint Self-Attention, to jointly predict future RGB observations, Scalar Affordance fields, Affordance Heatmaps, and continuous robot actions under a unified flow-matching objective. Human videos supervise all three future-World streams, whereas robot trajectories additionally provide action supervision, enabling transfer without human action labels or retargeting. Experiments on RoboCasa, CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D, and real-world manipulation demonstrate consistent gains over RGB-only and robot-data-only baselines. Under fixed robot supervision, RoboCasa performance improves monotonically as affordance-annotated human video scales. These results support affordance as an effective interface for both vision-language-action learning and human-to-robot transfer.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Beyond Explicit Intent: Discovering and Shaping Artistic Intent through Human-AI Co-Creation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Renye Yan, Jialun Zhong, Jikang Cheng, Yi Gao, Yanzeng Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper presents a human-AI co-creation framework that enhances artistic intent discovery and shaping by allowing artists to explore and refine preferences through interaction with generative AI.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Generative AI is becoming an important medium for artistic creation, yet existing interactions often assume that creators can specify intentions in advance and accurately communicate them through text prompts. Artistic intentions, however, may be vague, latent, or recognizable only after seeing concrete visual possibilities. We propose a human-AI co-creation paradigm beyond explicit intent expression. By expanding model exploration, we expose artists to diverse visual possibilities, allowing them to identify previously unarticulated preferences through observation, comparison, and selection. We then integrate artists' curatorial judgments into reinforcement learning, assigning different learning strengths based on preferences over generation trajectories, so recognized directions are more strongly reinforced and the model gradually adapts to individual aesthetics. This creates a continuous "explore-identify-shape-re-explore" loop in which artistic intent is progressively discovered, externalized, and shaped. Through three user studies, we examine latent-preference discovery, personalized preference alignment, and the externalization of vague, difficult-to-express creative intentions.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: RL Teaches VLMs Where to Attend but Not How to Perceive
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Ziqian Zhang, Junjie Liao, Zhining Zhang, Wentao Zhu
